The district's budget, its own funds, and what the town publishes about its schools.

Tier 1 · totalswhat was appropriated and what is left, by department

dese_ch70_formula school Tier 1 · totals fact 259 rows 1993–2026one row per district per fiscal year

The Chapter 70 formula term by term for every Massachusetts district, FY1993-FY2026: foundation enrollment, foundation budget, required local contribution, aid, required net school spending and what was actually spent. Thirty-four years. It answers a question nobody in town can currently put a number on -- does Lunenburg spend above or below the minimum the state requires -- and its FY2026 aid figure ties exactly to the town's own MUNIS revenue ledger.

THREE COLUMN NAMES IN THE SOURCE MEAN TWO THINGS EACH. required_nss is the workbook's column I, the formula's own arithmetic; required_nss_published is column J, what DESE publishes with carryover included, and the two differ in over a thousand district-years. ch70_aid and ch70_aid_after_penalties are columns H and M. AND nss_stage IS LOAD-BEARING: the source column is headed actualNSS for all thirty-four years, but FY2025 and FY2026 hold BUDGETED net school spending. Rule 1 -- a rate measured from an actual to a budget is partly growth and partly the step between the two. Publish the ratio to required as a measurement and never as a verdict: the required minimum is a floor, not a standard of adequacy. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and dese_ch70_statewide keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.

dese_circuit_breaker school Tier 1 · totals fact 147 rows 2006–2026one row per district per FISCAL year

State reimbursement for high-cost special education placements, FY2006-FY2026, split into instruction and tuition against transportation, with prior-year adjustments and relief payments separated -- so a year's receipt can be told apart from a year's entitlement. It also carries eligible_students_claimed, a count of CHILDREN.

KEYED ON FISCAL YEAR, NOT SCHOOL YEAR. Every other DESE table here is school year, and this repository has already had a fiscal-year type error that matched nothing silently. This is money the district RECEIVES and it does not appear in the general fund appropriation the town votes -- rule 11: a budget line that fell because circuit breaker rose is not a line that got cheaper. eligible_students_claimed counts CLAIMS, which is not the same set as the children in sources/data/placement-counts.csv. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and dese_ch70_statewide keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.

dese_enrollment school Tier 1 · totals fact 1,194 rows 1992–2026one row per organisation per school year

Enrollment by grade and by selected population -- English learner, low income, economically disadvantaged, high needs, students with disabilities -- per state, district and school, back to SY1992. The denominator for nearly every rate on this site.

Filter org_level. swd_cnt is a published count of students with disabilities and it agrees exactly with dese_sped_program for Lunenburg SY2026; it does NOT agree with the denominator the staffing ratios in dese_sped_indicator use, which is twelve lower in the same year. A per-pupil figure is a division by a count whose definition has to be stated with it -- DESE publishes at least four different counts of Lunenburg's children and none of them equal, see money_gaps.

dese_town_enrollment school Tier 1 · totals fact 1,488 rows 2014–2026one row per school year per town of residence per enrollment reason per enrolling district

Where a town's resident children actually go to school, and who arrives from where, SY2014-SY2026, by reason: school choice, charter, tuitioned in several ways, METCO, foster care. Both directions of the choice question, and the headcounts behind the choice dollars on the cherry sheet.

ONE TABLE FROM TWO DATASET IDS. DESE publishes vxt3-k35x as Sending and 8xyg-59b2 as Receiving; compared row by row they hold the IDENTICAL rows and differ only in column order, so they are one measurement published twice and are loaded once. Do not treat a net position drawn from this as resting on two agreeing sources. Filter on town for children leaving, on lea for children arriving; town='Lunenburg' AND lea='01620000' is the resident children who stay. SCOPED: every row about Lunenburg in either direction plus both directions for the six peers, because 74,878 statewide rows would take the published database past Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. The two source files were compared on all 74,878 rows before scoping, so the claim that they are one dataset published twice covers the whole publication.

Dollar amounts per budget LINE from the district's budget documents — no counts, no people. Each figure carries the stage it represents (proposed / settled / actual) and, for FY27, which of four whole budget scenarios it belongs to. FY2014–FY2027, 9,503 figures, plus a flag where two documents state different amounts for the same line-year.

Split on stage AND variant. FY27 carries four whole budgets.

dese_ap school Tier 2 · categories fact 9,906 rowsone row per publication per organisation per student group per AP subject per school year

Advanced Placement PARTICIPATION and PERFORMANCE for Lunenburg, SY2007-SY2025: how many students sat AP, how many tests, the distribution of tests per student, and the score distribution 1-5. Extracted from two 174MB statewide DESE workbooks filtered to LEA 01620000.

kind separates the PARTICIPATION extract from the PERFORMANCE extract and they are different quantities in one file. stu_grp OVERLAPS -- "All Students" sits beside race, gender and selected-population groups and they may never be summed. org_type separates district from school. A subject absent for a year is not established to be a published zero; do not read it as one without checking the extractor. Tests are not students: tests_taken_cnt counts sittings and test_takers_cnt counts children. kind is a SECOND level column: participation and performance are two publications in one table and each leaves the other’s figure columns NULL. District and school rows are the SAME SIZE here (4,953 each) because Lunenburg’s AP is all at one school, so summing them doubles silently.

dese_attrition school Tier 2 · categories fact 1,061 rowsone row per organisation per student group per school year, carrying a rate per grade

The share of students who LEFT, by grade, SY2010-SY2026 -- which is the dataset that answers "which grades are students leaving in, over time". Every figure is a PERCENTAGE, not a count.

RATES, NOT COUNTS -- g01_pct through g11_pct and grd_all are percentages, so they may not be summed or averaged across grades without weighting by the enrolment in each grade. stu_grp OVERLAPS ("All Students" beside race and selected-population groups). A rate off a small grade cohort moves violently; read the year-by-year before concluding a trend. Attrition counts leaving for any reason, so it does not separate a move out of town from a transfer to another school.

dese_ch70_aid_factor school Tier 2 · categories fact 155 rows 2007–2026one row per district per fiscal year

The aid build-up, term by term, FY2007 on: every increment the Chapter 70 formula adds between the foundation budget and the aid actually paid, and every reduction it applies. This is what lets anybody model how the aid RESPONDS to a change in enrollment rather than assuming it moves linearly.

level separates the state row from the districts. Its ch70_aid agrees with dese_ch70_formula in every district-year they share, checked on every build -- they are two sheets of one workbook, not two sources. The increments are the formula's own machinery and several are zero in most years by design; a zero here is a term that did not apply, not a missing figure. SCOPED to Lunenburg, its six peers and the state row, because the published database has to stay under Cloudflare's 25MB per-asset limit. Every identity the extract asserts is asserted across ALL districts before the scope is applied, and dese_ch70_statewide keeps the all-district comparison as a distribution.

dese_class_size school Tier 2 · categories fact 3,160 rowsone row per organisation per subject per school year

HOW MANY CLASSES RAN, and how full they were, by school and by subject, SY2011-SY2025. The only table here that counts what was TAUGHT rather than who was employed, what was appropriated or how many children enrolled -- so it is what answers "did the cuts change what a child can take" without reaching for teacher FTE, which cannot tell four Spanish sections from two.

THREE SPLITS BEFORE ANY SUM. org_type separates the DISTRICT rollup from its own schools. subj = "All" is a rollup of the 25 named subjects beside it. And the fifteen subjects prefixed "CH74 - " are a SECOND, PARALLEL classification -- Chapter 74 vocational programme areas, every Lunenburg row of them zero -- which are not part of the subject total. THE THREE FIGURE COLUMNS ARE THREE QUANTITIES: tot_clss_cnt is classes that ran, avg_clss_cnt is DESE’s own average class size (seats over classes), and tot_stu_cnt is DISTINCT students who took the subject -- NOT seats, and not the product of the other two. sy is the school year ENDING and equals fy in every other DESE table here; it keeps the publisher’s own column name. AND A SCHOOL NAME IS NOT A FIXED SCHOOL: Lunenburg High held grades 8-12 from SY2013 to SY2016 and grades 9-12 either side, so join dese_enrollment for the grade span before comparing two years. The demographic percentage columns OVERLAP each other and may never be added. Two school-years report an average class size no primary school can have -- 87.1 in SY2011 and 36.5 in SY2022, both Lunenburg Primary -- so the elementary series is not trendable.

dese_educator_workforce school Tier 2 · categories fact 840 rows 2021–2023one row per district per race/ethnicity per job class per school year

HEADCOUNT by job class -- Administrator, Teacher, Paraprofessional, Other Licensed, Other Non-Licensed -- with hires and retention, SY2021-SY2023. The only DESE table here that counts administrators and paraprofessionals as PEOPLE rather than as FTE or as dollars.

race_level is the level column and getting it wrong doubles every figure. All Educators is a TOTAL row sitting beside the seven reported races; summing the whole job class gives exactly twice the truth, and this project's own notes recorded 118 paraprofessionals and 38 administrators for SY2023 that way when the file holds 59 and 19. There is no all-job-classes row, so a district total is the sum of the five race_level='all' rows and no published figure states it. Headcount is not FTE: a half-time director and a principal are one each. Three years is a thin series on a base of tens, and a reclassification would look identical to a change in staffing.

dese_function_expenditure school Tier 2 · categories fact 6,930 rows 2009–2025one row per district per year per function code per level

DESE's spending by function code with the GENERAL FUND and GRANTS/REVOLVING money in separate columns, SY2009-SY2025, for Lunenburg and its six peers. The only published split of the two in this archive: Lunenburg SY2025 shows $478,097 of grant and revolving money against function 2330, Paraprofessionals, beside $1,338,477 of general fund.

Filter on level before aggregating ANYTHING. The source puts rollups beside detail and nothing in its column names says which is which -- summing every Lunenburg SY2025 row gives $117,996,913 against an in-district total of $27,903,187. level='total' is TTPP; level='rollup' is IIII and OODD; level='category' is the ten in-district categories plus ODTR and COMM; level='detail' is the printed function codes, plus TUIT, which has no category row. ODTR is already inside OODD -- adding it again double counts -- and its detail is only ever code 9130, a component and not the whole, which is what reconciles='partial' means. This is DESE's definition of spending, all funds, and it is NOT the town's appropriation; it must never be subtracted from one. A function code is not a budget line and not a post, so this bounds the funding-source question rather than settling it.

dese_sped_indicator school Tier 2 · categories fact 4,860 rows 2017–2026one row per district per grade group per student group per indicator per school year

Special education indicators SY2017-SY2026: the context counts, the special education staffing ratios per 100 students with disabilities, and the outcome, assessment and postsecondary measures, each with students with disabilities set beside students without.

Three things. (1) grades_level says all or subset and THE SUBSETS OVERLAP -- Grade 10 is inside Grades 9-12 is inside K-12 -- so no sum across grades means anything. (2) denominator_cnt is the population the percentage is OF; the indicator's own figure is measure_cnt, and on the SPECIAL EDUCATION STAFF rows measure_cnt is the students-with-disabilities denominator while measure_pct is the FTE per 100 of them. (3) value_type says whether a row is a percentage, an average, an FTE or an FTE per 100 -- read it before doing arithmetic. The staffing ratios times the count are what produce the unresolved $69,161 per paraprofessional FTE; see money_gaps. printing is part of the key -- DESE publishes a handful of these rows twice -- so collapse on it before aggregating.

dese_sped_movement school Tier 2 · categories fact 684 rows 2019–2025one row per district per grade group per school year

Caseload movement: how many children entered special education services in a year and how many left. The dynamic behind the spending line that a headcount alone cannot show. SY2019-SY2025.

TWO TRAPS. repeats_prior_year is yes where all four figures exactly equal the same district's previous year -- Lunenburg's SY2024 and SY2025 are such a pair, and four independently counted quantities landing identically two years running is not plausible where a row carried forward is. Never sum two such years as two years of movement. And grade_rows_sum is NOT enrolled_cnt: the grade rows are not the K-12 row broken down, because the Grade 12 row is a fraction of the size of the others. What the residual is has not been established.

dese_sped_program school Tier 2 · categories fact 2,403 rows 2020–2026one row per district per indicator category per indicator per school year

What the students with disabilities are: disability type, race, gender, grade span, in district against out of district, placement, and the special education FTE ratios. SY2020-SY2026. It carries a PUBLISHED count of students with disabilities, which used to be reachable here only by multiplying a percentage by enrollment.

indicator_level is total or member and every category carries its own total row. Three categories do not behave like the others: Placement runs SHORT of its own total because its four members are IN-DISTRICT placements and children placed out of district appear in the total and in none of them; Disability Type is a collapsed rendering of Disability Type All with several disabilities folded into Other Disability, so adding the two counts every child twice; and Special Education FTEs per 100 SWDs is a RATIO despite sitting in the same column and despite value_type saying Percent on every row of this file. printing is part of the key: 95 rows are published twice, most of them the same district under two different names (Ayer Shirley and Ayer Shirley School District share one org code). Collapse on it before aggregating.

dese_teacher_grade_subject school Tier 2 · categories fact 8,467 rows 2008–2026one row per organisation per subject per school year, FTE split across six grade bands

Teacher FTE by grade band AND subject AND school. This breaks a limit recorded here as structural: the town's staff rosters give grade detail with no FTE, and DESE elsewhere gives FTE with no grade. This gives both.

Two level columns and both matter: org_level and subject_level. Summing every subject for one organisation counts each teacher about three times over -- the build asserts that it would, so a lost level column fails there rather than in your query. agrees_with_teacher_subject is written on the All rows only and says whether this dataset and dese_teacher_subject state the same total FTE for that organisation; where they do not, BOTH are kept and neither corrects the other. A SUBJECT ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE for an organisation and year we hold is a PUBLISHED ZERO, not a gap -- rows where every grade band and the total are nought are not written, and they outnumber the real rows two to one. That is the opposite of the usual reading here, which is why it is said twice. printing is part of the key: DESE publishes the same organisation, subject and year twice with different figures in a small number of cases, and both are kept.

stated_cuts school Tier 2 · categories fact 193 rows 2020, 2021, 2025, 2026, 2027one row per reduction or restoration NAMED in a district budget document

What the district said in writing it was cutting, cycle by cycle, FY2020 to FY2027 — the position, the school, the FTE and the dollar figure WHERE THE DOCUMENT PRINTS THEM, and the district’s own stated consequence, quoted. Every row is a CLAIM: a reduction list is a document somebody assembled to argue for a budget (rule 13a), so basis is stated on all 193 rows and none of it is evidence that a post was removed. direction separates a reduction from a restoration or an addition; conditional_on records that FY2025 has TWO lists, one for each outcome of a ballot question that passed. /cut-register sets DESE’s teacher counts beside it.

NEVER aggregate across documents without splitting on doc_date: a position named on three lists in one cycle is three rows, because the register keeps every draft. Most rows carry no FTE and no amount because the document printed none, and a blank is an absence in the SOURCE rather than in the extract.

teacher_salary_schedules school Tier 2 · categories fact 5,231 rows 2016–2028one row per printed cell of a teacher salary schedule: district, schedule, step, lane

What each district's teachers' contract PRINTS as the pay scale, by step and lane, for Lunenburg and the districts it is compared with -- the question an average salary cannot answer, because an average also carries who is employed at which step. read says how each cell was read (text layer, OCR confirmed by a second reading, or by eye off the page) and flag names any cell that fails a check: rising along steps and across lanes, and equal to the previous year times the increase the contract states.

A SCALE, not pay: no headcount by step or lane is here, and longevity, stipends and degree add-ons paid outside the grid are not in it -- Lunenburg's own longevity adds to step 13. Lane names and step counts differ by district, so compare like lanes by name, never by position. fy repeats within a document where two schedules apply in one year; split on schedule. Several DESE filings are expired contracts: check contract_period and teacher_salary_schedule_docs before calling a figure current.

v_line_budget_vs_actual school Tier 2 · categories view 4,506 rows 2014–2027one row per budget line per year, stages pivoted into columns

Budget against what was actually spent, one row per line per year: the settled budget, the proposed budget and the actual (stage restated) side by side, FY2014-FY2027. This is the starting point for asking which lines underspend or overspend their budget. Scenario figures are excluded -- variant = '' only.

documents_disagree IS WRONG AS A BUDGET-VS-ACTUAL FLAG. It is MAX() across ALL stages, so a line where two documents disagree about the PROPOSED column is reported as a line whose budget and actual are disputed. Of the disagreeing line-year-stage cells, 254 are proposed against 45 settled and 35 restated, and the view flags 322 of its 4,506 rows on that basis. scripts/build_variance_charts.py does NOT use this view: it pivots the flag PER STAGE and records that the difference moved every figure on the budget-vs-actual page by about 15%. Do the same, or read the flag from budget_figure with a stage filter. Separately: a NULL column is a line the documents state at only one stage, not a zero.

v_workbook_budget_vs_actual school Tier 2 · categories view 245 rows 2025–2025one row per worksheet row per year, budget column against actual column

Budget against actual TAKEN FROM ONE DOCUMENT -- the district's own workbook, matching a budget or final_budget column to the actual column on the same worksheet row, same year, same document. under_budget is budget minus actual. 245 lines, FY2025.

The join is doc_id AND row AND fy, so both figures come from the SAME sheet and the same printed row -- which is the like-for-like comparison, but it also means the coverage is whatever that one workbook prints, not the district's whole budget. row_kind = 'line' excludes subtotals, so these do not add to any printed total. under_budget is a difference between two columns of one document; it is not a statement about what was appropriated. And rule 13a applies: a hand-built workbook is an argument, not a printout from the books -- check document_basis for what produced this one.

Rule 13: quotes a coordinate, so a figure can be traced to its cell.

dese_ch70_statewide school Tier 3 · accounts fact 122 rows 1993–2026one row per fiscal year per measure, across every Massachusetts district

Where Lunenburg sits among every Massachusetts district on four ratios: net school spending as a share of what the state requires, Chapter 70 aid per foundation pupil, the required local contribution as a share of the foundation budget, and circuit breaker claim per eligible student. Min, quartiles, median, max, Lunenburg's own figure and its rank.

Read the denominator before quoting a rank -- districts is it, and it counts only districts that reported the measure that year. basis says on every row what the ratio is OF, because each is a division by a count or a dollar whose definition has to travel with it: foundation enrollment is not a headcount of children in the buildings, and the circuit breaker rows are FISCAL year where the rest are the Chapter 70 fiscal year. Publish the share-of-required as a measurement and never as a verdict -- the required minimum is a floor, not a standard of adequacy, and a district above it is not thereby adequately funded.

dese_function_statewide school Tier 3 · accounts fact 1,438 rows 2009–2025one row per year per function code per level, across every Massachusetts district

Where Lunenburg sits among all Massachusetts districts on per-pupil spending, function by function, SY2009-SY2025 -- min, quartiles, median, max, Lunenburg's own figure and its rank. Also the statewide dollar totals and the share of each function paid by grants and revolving money rather than the general fund.

Read the denominator before quoting a rank. districts is the denominator and it INCLUDES charter and virtual districts, which are in DESE's file and are not municipal school districts. per_pupil_basis says on every row whether a per-pupil figure exists at all: DESE prints 0 against every out-of-district row, so the quartiles are blank there rather than a median of zeros. Filter on level here too -- a category and its own detail are separate rows.

dese_teacher_subject school Tier 3 · accounts fact 5,527 rows 2008–2026one row per organisation per subject per school year

Teacher FTE by subject, with the share licensed, the share teaching in field, the share experienced and the students-per-teacher ratio, SY2008-SY2026.

teacher_fte IS AN FTE even though DESE names the column TCHR_CNT. Filter subject_level: all is every teacher, group is Core-All Subjects and Total Non-Core Academic Subjects which are groups of the subjects beside them, and the members therefore DO NOT PARTITION -- summing subjects double counts. students_per_teacher is parsed from the sentence DESE prints, which is kept beside it in student_teacher_ratio_printed. A SUBJECT ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE for an organisation and year we hold is a PUBLISHED ZERO, not a gap: rows with no FTE at all are not written, and they outnumber the real ones.

all is All/All Teachers. group is Core-All Subjects and Total Non-Core Academic Subjects, which are groups of the subjects beside them, so the members of this column DO NOT PARTITION. Summing subjects counts a teacher about three times.

DESE names the source column TCHR_CNT. It is not a headcount: the state row is 76,718.6. And FTE here is EPIMS FTE, defined as the share of a workday given to an ASSIGNMENT rather than to a person, so it cannot be divided into a budget line to get a cost per employee.

munis_school_journal school Tier 3 · accounts fact 49,043 rowsone row per journal line: every posting behind every school account, general fund AND every school special fund (grants, circuit breaker, revolving, school choice, lunch, gifts), FY2023 period 0 to FY2026 period 13

Who the schools paid, when, from which fund and account, and why the books moved: every invoice (API), payroll posting (PRJ), purchase order and its liquidation (POE/POL/POM), budget entry (BUC original, BUA transfer), year-end reclassification (GEN) and receipt (CRP). The all-funds view no budget document gives: a cost leaving the general fund for a grant shows as both halves. Our redacted reading of the Town's 1,744-page MUNIS journal report; the raw is private.

REDACTED under TJ's rule: recipients of school services (children, and families acting for them) are masked with every residue; providers and vendors are named. vendor = 'individual (redacted)' is a masked family payee, blank = the Town printed no payee; name_basis says why a person is shown. posts_to splits actual from encumbrance from budget -- sum only one. Payroll is dollars by account, not people. FY2026's year-end close is not posted in this run, so FY26 encumbrances are still open. Every line is NET (CLAUDE.md rule 11).

v_budget_disagreement school view 1,502 rows 2014–2027one row per disagreeing reading (line, year, stage, variant, source document)

Where two documents state DIFFERENT dollar amounts for the same budget line and year -- both readings kept, each with the document it came from and the spread between them. This is the table to read when you want to know which budget figures are disputed and by how much, and which document said what. A pass-through of line_history_disagreements with the numbers cast to REAL.

Nothing here is resolved: which document is right is usually not established, and is_kept records which reading the model took, not which is correct. Rows are READINGS, not lines -- counting rows counts documents, so use COUNT(DISTINCT line_key || fy) for a count of disputed line-years. Split on stage and variant: 254 of the disagreeing line-year-stage cells are at stage proposed and only 45 settled and 35 restated, so a disagreement is most often two proposals, not a contested actual.

Normalisation differs between budget_figure and workbook_figure — joining them on line_key matches only a fraction. Join on the normalised label instead.

PEOPLE -- every name the town printed in a school staff roster, FY2011-FY2025, with the school, the page, the job title exactly as printed (role_raw) and our classification of it into a role category and grade. This is the dataset for counting how many teachers, paraprofessionals or secretaries a school listed in a year.

A COUNT OF NAMES IS NOT A STAFFING LEVEL. There is NO FTE, so a 0.4 music teacher and a full-timer are one row each; NO FUNDING SOURCE, which is the question rule 11 says actually matters; no salary; and the roster is a point in time undated within the year. role_category and role_grade are OUR judgement (see classified_by), not the town's words -- role_raw is the town's words. The join to role_classification is a LEFT JOIN, so an unclassified title would arrive NULL; none is NULL today. position_legacy is the superseded column and is kept only so an older query still resolves.

census_acs town Tier 1 · totals fact 889 rowsone row per ACS table per variable per geography per 5-year vintage

WHO LIVES IN LUNENBURG -- the only table here that measures RESIDENTS rather than children, dollars or documents. Age by sex (B01001), households by presence of a child under 18 (B11005), median household income by age of householder (B19049) and owner against renter (B25003) for Lunenburg town, plus median household income for EVERY Massachusetts municipality (B19013) so the town can be ranked rather than described. Two 5-year vintages, 2018 (2014-2018) and 2023 (2019-2023), which do not overlap.

EVERY FIGURE IS A SAMPLE ESTIMATE WITH A MARGIN AND THE MARGINS ARE WIDE. This is not a DESE count: 1,568 children means 1,568, while households with a child under 18 is 1,477 +/- 198. Never quote an estimate without moe; two figures whose intervals overlap are NOT different, and a difference between the two vintages smaller than the combined margin is not a change. level IS THE ROLLUP GUARD -- town is Lunenburg alone and municipality is the 350-town statewide income column, and reading one for the other turns a town figure into a statewide one. THE NEGATIVE VALUES IN estimate_raw AND moe_raw ARE SENTINELS, NOT FIGURES: -666666666 is no estimate, -222222222 and -333333333 are no computable margin, -555555555 is an estimate CONTROLLED to an independent total and is not a margin of zero. estimate and moe are NULL wherever one of those was published and usable says so. A rank off this column is arithmetic, not a ranking: 205 of the 350 municipalities have an income interval overlapping Lunenburg's. And it counts households with a child under 18, which is a CEILING on households with a child in the Lunenburg public schools -- see money_gaps.

dese_ch70_contribution town Tier 2 · categories fact 7,040 rows 2007–2026one row per MUNICIPALITY per fiscal year

The municipal side of the Chapter 70 formula: equalized valuation, income, the effort each implies, the target local contribution and how the required contribution was arrived at. This is where the town's ability to pay is computed, and it is the half of the formula the school budget never shows.

A DIFFERENT GRAIN FROM EVERY OTHER CHAPTER 70 TABLE HERE: a row is a TOWN, not a district, and lea_number is the workbook's own municipal key rather than a DESE org code. For a regional district several towns contribute to one district, so this must not be joined one to one with dese_ch70_formula. AND THE TOWN'S REQUIRED CONTRIBUTION IS NOT THE DISTRICT'S: for FY2026 Lunenburg the town figure is $14,605,342 and the Lunenburg school district figure in dese_ch70_formula is $13,334,631, because a town also contributes to any regional district it belongs to. Every district is kept here rather than the seven-district peer scope the other Chapter 70 tables use, because a town in a regional district has a contribution row and no district row and scoping by district would drop exactly those.

Families by layout: cash-by-fund, investments-by-fund, investments-composition, and 1986's cash-reconciliation-schedule, cash-composition, investments-schedule, trust-custody-composition.

v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in column_meaning from the printed header. edition is the book's printed year (1986), never FY1986. Split on status. A second printing of the stock treasurers_cash holds, by another officer: never sum the two. Split on table_family.

columntypewhat it is
datasetTEXTWhich extract family this row belongs to.
fyINTEGERFiscal year, ending 30 June. FY2026 runs 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. year
INTEGER everywhere except grant_award/grants_history (a multi-year ESSER award) and rate_register (one rate with no year).
editionTEXTWhich annual town report the row was read from, as that report names itself.
FY2016 has TWO editions — the report and an addendum. Summing on fy rather than edition counts that year twice.
pageTEXTThe page number printed on the page, not the PDF's index.
The two differ by a cover offset that is not constant across years.
panelTEXTWhich block of the page this row came from, where a page prints several tables.
Two panels on one page have different column rulers. Summing across panels mixes them.
groupTEXTThe department heading the row sits under, as printed.
A heading governs every row below it until the next one.
labelTEXTThe row's name, as printed.
Not a key. MUNIS truncates to ten characters, so MS GUIDANC and HS GUIDANC collide.
label_missingTEXTThe row's label did not survive extraction.
The figures may still be good. A missing label is not a missing row.
kindTEXTWhat sort of row or record this is.
Meaning differs by table — see the per-table entry.
row_checkTEXTWhether the row satisfies an identity the table itself states.
derived_cellTEXTA cell we computed from the row's own other cells, recorded here and NEVER written into a v column.
An inference kept out of the readings, on purpose.
table_familyTEXTWhich printed table shape this row came from.
line_noTEXTPosition of the row on the page, counting from the top.
Positional, so it identifies a row within a page and nothing beyond it.
columns_as_printedTEXTThe column headings of this table, verbatim, as that page prints them.
This is what says which printed column v1 actually is. It is the only thing that does.
v1TEXTORDINAL, NOT A COLUMN NAME: the first column of THIS PAGE that held figures. dollars
The ruler is built per page, so v1 on one page and v1 on the next can be different printed columns. Read column_meaning. Summing v1 down a run adds one page's APPROPRIATED to another's TOTAL EXPENDED.

balance_sheet school + town Tier 1 · totals fact 1,699 rows 1987–2022one row per line per fund column per year

What the town HOLDS, read from the COMBINED BALANCE SHEET — assets, liabilities and fund equity across six fund columns (general, special revenue, enterprise, capital project, trust and agency, long-term debt). Everything else in this archive measures money MOVING; this is the only table that measures what is sitting there.

Read from the page, like special_revenue_read. It is trusted because three checks hold: each column foots to its own printed total, the sheet's identity (liabilities + fund equity = assets) holds per column, and special revenue + enterprise fund equity ties to the special revenue schedule's carried-forward total — an INDEPENDENT document. One printed sheet does not balance itself (FY2019 trust and agency, $657,297.35 apart); that is the town's print, recorded not corrected.

enterprise_balance_sheet school + town Tier 1 · totals fact 114 rows 2024–2025one row per line per fund column per printing per year

What the four ENTERPRISE funds hold at 30 June — Sewer, Water, Solid Waste and PEG Access, side by side, with a memorandum-only total column. Read from the COMBINING BALANCE SHEET — ENTERPRISE FUNDS, which is the only balance sheet FY2024 and FY2025 print; neither report contains the town-wide combined balance sheet balance_sheet holds for FY2011–FY2023.

RATEPAYER MONEY. Sewer and water user charges, betterments, trash fees and cable franchise money — none of it is available to the town's general operations and none of it is a tax dollar. This is NOT an extension of balance_sheet: that table's enterprise value is one of six fund-type COLUMNS on a different sheet, and the two must never be unioned. FY2024 prints the same sheet TWICE (printed pages 21 and 28), so printing is 1 or 2 and must be collapsed on before anything is summed — summing across it doubles the money. FY2024's memorandum column is $102,000.00 out on two offsetting lines; that is the town's print, recorded not corrected. Only cells that print a figure are recorded; the sheet's 0.00 and '-' template cells are not rows here.

v_fund_year school + town Tier 1 · totals view 61 rows 2026–2026one row per fund per year per period

Every town FUND on one line: what came in (revenue), what went out (spent, salaries plus other expenditure added together), and what the fund is holding at the end (closing_balance), with the fund's name, kind and what restricts it. This is where to look for money that is not the general fund -- revolving funds, grants, the circuit breaker, trusts.

opening_balance is not carried here and is NULL for all 61 funds in fund_activity anyway, so closing_balance cannot be reconciled to a starting point. FY2026 period 9 only -- a balance at 31 March, not a year end. spent FOLDS salaries and expenditure together; query fund_activity if you need them apart. The join to fund is a LEFT JOIN, so name, kind and restriction can be NULL for a fund the fund dimension does not carry.

peg_access school + town Tier 2 · categories fact 110 rows 2015–2025one row per printed expense line per year

What the town's PEG Access / Public Access Cable operation spent, line by line, FY2015-FY2025, read from the expense table each annual town report prints. From FY2020 the report also prints a % of Expense column and it is recorded here beside the amount.

CABLE FRANCHISE MONEY, not tax money. Comcast pays it under the Town's cable licence; from FY2020 it sits in a PEG Access enterprise fund established under MGL c.44 s53F1/2 and is appropriated by its own Town Meeting article. None of it is available to general operations. The line LIST changes: Insurance disappears after FY2020 and Indirect Costs appears, so a line-by-line series across that boundary is comparing different things. FY2017's ten lines add to 450.01 MORE than that report's own printed TOTAL; the total is what the rest of the record uses. Join to peg_access_printed_totals for the total each year actually prints -- never sum these rows and call it the year's expenses without saying so.

v_burn school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 759 rows 2026–2026one row per account per year per non-final period

Spending PACE part-way through the year: how much of the revised budget has been expended, how much is expended-plus-encumbered, and pace_gap -- the committed share minus the share of the year elapsed. A positive pace_gap is a line committed ahead of the calendar. Over ledger_snapshot at every period fiscal_period marks not final.

IT DOES NOT FILTER account_type, so 224 of its 983 rows are REVENUE accounts, whose amounts are stored negative -- spent_share on those is not a burn rate at all (PS TUITION reads 7.53). Filter a.account_type = 'expense' yourself, which means joining account again. pace_gap is a calendar proxy, not a schedule: it assumes even spending across twelve months, and nothing here establishes that any line spends evenly. fiscal_period marks period 12 as not final, so period-12 rows carry year_elapsed = 1.0. Two grains: period 9 carries department roll-ups AND accounts, period 12 accounts only.

v_function_budget_vs_ledger school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 46 rows 2026–2026one row per DESE function code per year per period

The town's ledger rolled up to DESE FUNCTION CODE -- revised, expended and encumbered summed per function, with a count of the accounts behind it and a count of the district budget lines whose function_group starts with the same four characters. v_interfund school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 12 rows 2026–2026one row per interfund transfer-in revenue account per year per period

TRANSFERS BETWEEN FUNDS as they appear on the revenue side -- money moving into a fund from another fund rather than from a taxpayer or the state. v_revenue filtered to objects beginning 490 plus object 499900; 12 rows, FY2026 period 9.

This is money the town moved from one of its own pockets to another. Adding it to tax and state aid double-counts, because the same dollar is a receipt in one fund and a disbursement in the other -- and the disbursement side is not in this view. The membership test is an OBJECT-CODE PATTERN (490% or 499900) written into the view, not a classification anybody published; an interfund transfer coded to another object would not appear.

v_revenue school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 224 rows 2026–2026one row per revenue account per year per period

MONEY COMING IN -- every revenue account in the town's MUNIS books with the sign flipped to positive: what was budgeted, what has been received, what is still to come, and the percent received. Property tax, state aid, local receipts, fees, transfers in. FY2026 at period 9, 224 accounts.

THE SIGNS ARE NEGATED HERE. ledger_snapshot stores revenue negative and this view multiplies by -1, so figures are positive in the view and negative in the table it reads -- never mix the two in one sum. pct_received is computed from the RAW columns, not the negated ones. A part-year snapshot: 74.5% of the tax levy received at 31 March is the calendar, not a shortfall. still_to_come is the ledger's available, negated -- it is what has not been collected yet, not a forecast.

v_revenue_classified school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 224 rows 2026–2026one row per revenue account per year per period, with our class attached

Money coming in, grouped by WHERE IT COMES FROM: property tax levy, state aid, local receipts, one-time money, transfers in. v_revenue left-joined to our money_classification rows for revenue accounts. This is the view behind the revenue side of the money-flow diagrams.

THE CLASS IS A DEFAULT, NOT ALWAYS A MEASUREMENT. Any account with no classification row falls through to local / 'Local receipts' by COALESCE, and 171 of the 224 rows carry that label -- so 'Local receipts' means 'classified as local OR not classified at all' and the two cannot be told apart from this view. Join money_classification yourself if you need to know which. The classification is ours, recorded so it can be argued with; how and why in money_classification carry the basis. Amounts are the negated (positive) figures from v_revenue.

v_spending_classified school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 67 rows 2026–2026one row per town department per year per period

Money going out, grouped by HOW MUCH CONTROL the town has over it: assessed, bargained, committed, delegated, transfer or discretionary, with how that was established (control_how). Voted, revised and expended per department. 67 departments, FY2026 period 9. This is the view behind the question 'how much of the budget could the town actually change'.

discretionary IS THE RESIDUAL AND IT IS NOT A FINDING. 49 of the 67 departments carry control = discretionary with control_how = residual, which means nobody classified them -- not that the town established they are discretionary. STATE AID as the town's own books record it -- Chapter 70 and the rest of the cherry sheet, budgeted against received. v_revenue filtered to objects beginning 45; 29 accounts, FY2026 period 9. Chapter 70 is the single account CH 70 AID, $9,229,410 budgeted in FY2026.

CHAPTER 70 IS NOT STATE AID. It is one account in this view, and the rest of the cherry sheet -- Unrestricted General Government Aid and everything else -- is not school money. Summing this view gives total state aid, which is what model/finance.py grows; do not call that figure Chapter 70, and do not call Chapter 70 the town's state aid. v_transfer_history school + town Tier 3 · accounts view 759 rows 2026–2026one row per account per year per period

Money MOVED BETWEEN LINES after the budget was voted: the original appropriation, the cumulative transfers into or out of it, and the revised figure, per account. moved_since_last is meant to be the change in transfers since the previous period.

moved_since_last IS EFFECTIVELY EMPTY AND SHOULD NOT BE USED: it is non-NULL on 2 of 983 rows, because the LAG needs the same account_id at two periods and ledger_snapshot holds none -- period 9 carries the department roll-ups plus 277 accounts and period 12 carries a different 635 accounts. The two non-NULL values are duplicate rows within period 9, not a movement between periods. transfers itself is real and cumulative to the snapshot date, not per-period. The view does not filter account_type, so 224 revenue accounts are included, and their amounts are stored NEGATIVE and are not negated here as they are in v_revenue. It mixes department roll-ups with detail accounts -- filter level before summing.

dese_teacher_salaries state Tier 2 · categories fact 6,068 rows 2009–2025one row per district per school year (fy = the school year: 2025 is 2024-25)

DESE's AVERAGE TEACHER SALARY, teacher FTE and teachers per 100 FTE students for EVERY district in the state, SY2009-SY2025, as DESE's District Expenditures by Spending Category table prints them -- so Lunenburg can be set beside the districts the district itself named (comparison_sets), not only the ones selected in RADAR. Tied to dese_radar wherever both hold a year, by scripts/extract_dese_teacher_salaries.py.

The AVERAGE IS PRINTED ONLY FROM 2018; earlier rows carry FTE and an empty average, which is DESE not printing it, not a zero. An average is the scale times the seniority and credentials of whoever is employed, over FTE: it is NOT a pay scale (teacher_salary_schedules is) and not what any teacher is paid. Values are TEXT as printed; CAST before comparing.

v_provenance archive view 40 rowsone row per source document per kind of fact

Which DOCUMENT every money fact came out of, and how many rows it produced: the ledger rows, the budget figures and the workbook figures, each grouped by doc_id and joined to the document's archive path, what produced its figures (basis) and whether our copy still matches the publisher's (copy_state). The answer to 'where did this number come from' at the document level.

A count of ROWS, not of dollars -- a document with 1,148 figures is not therefore more authoritative than one with 12. basis is rule 13a's distinction (a printout from the accounting system versus a sheet somebody assembled) and it is what decides how much weight a figure carries, not the row count. copy_state is NULL where verify_source_copies.py has not checked that document. How this is arranged

Grouped by whose money it is, because that is the question people arrive with. Two other facets ride along as badges on every table.

badgewhat it tells you
Tier 1 · totalsWhat was appropriated and what is left, by department. Not which category, not which school, not which fund paid.
Tier 2 · categoriesWhether guidance, special education or transport is over — and whether the town's books and the district's budget agree on a code. Not which school inside a category: names truncate at ten characters, so MS GUIDANC and HS GUIDANC are both 2710.
Tier 3 · accountsWhat one account spent, and how much came in per fund.
fact dimensionHow the table is built. Facts carry the figures; dimensions say what a key means and are joined to, never summed.
the spineThe three grains everything else describes, extracts or checks.

There is a tier below 3, and no report reaches it. Which revenue paid which expense. That is the grey edge in the join map, and it is why this archive measures appropriations and says so.

The columns you cannot leave out

None of these raises an error when omitted. Each returns a number that is the sum of two different things, which is why every one of them has been got wrong here at least once.

columninwhat happens if you omit it
statusannual report extractschecked, check failed, no check. Summing across them mixes verified figures with unverified ones.
levelaccount, ledger_snapshotdepartment roll-ups sit in the same table as their own detail. Summing both adds the budget to itself.
account_typeaccountRevenue is stored NEGATIVE. Omitting it once made the town’s whole budget compute as minus $997,871.
periodledger_snapshotTwo periods are two different MUNIS reports of the same year, not two halves of it.
stagebudget_figureproposed, settled, actual. Rule 1: a rate measured across stages is partly growth and partly the step between them.
variantbudget_figureFY27 has four whole budgets — Balanced, Core, Level Service, Restoration. Without this you sum all four.
v1 … v8annual report extractsORDINALS, not column names: the first column of THAT PAGE that held figures. Summing v1 down a run adds one page’s APPROPRIATED to another’s TOTAL EXPENDED.

And one that is now fixed. fy was stored as TEXT in 44 tables and INTEGER in 18, so WHERE fy = 2023 answered against a third of the database and returned zero rows, with no error, against the rest. It is INTEGER everywhere now except three documented exceptions, and check_fy_types in build_db.py fails the build if a new table arrives without it.

Two databases, and they are not always the same one. Everything printed on this page — row counts, samples, coverage — is read from the LOCAL sources/data/lunenburg.db when the page is built. Open full table queries {api_base}, a copy pushed to Cloudflare D1 that can lag behind. Point it elsewhere with ?api=<base-url> on this page's own URL, or set LUNENBURG_API before building. If a table opens empty, or the button reports that it does not exist, that copy has not been pushed yet: python3 scripts/sync_d1.py. This is stated rather than hidden because two sources that usually agree are the ones that mislead when they stop.

Views — the joins already written for you

A view is the safe way to ask a question that needs two tables. Each one carries the splitting columns above in its own WHERE, so it cannot be got wrong the way a hand-written join can.

What this database cannot tell you

Read from money_gaps, so this list is data rather than a thing somebody remembered to write down. Each is a question the published documents do not close.

sidewhat is missingwhy it cannot be answered
comparisonDo two districts put the same purchase on the same side of the line, so that their per-pupil figures compare like for like?DESE’s per-pupil figure counts functions 1000-5000 and leaves out capital (7000) and debt service (8000); its expenditures-by-function file carries no 6000, 7000 or 8000 row for any district, so no district’s figure contains capital. But the line between counted and capital is a coding rule, and DESE’s FY2025 End of Year Report form draws it: instructional equipment, “including vocational equipment and science lab equipment irrespective of unit cost”, goes in 2420 and is counted; non-instructional equipment over $5,000 and extraordinary maintenance over $150,000 a project go in 7000 and are not. Whether every district applies that rule the same way cannot be seen: DESE publishes each district’s reported totals, not the purchases behind them. So a difference between two districts on an equipment or maintenance line may be spending, or may be coding. — closes: each district’s own End of Year Financial Report workbook with its 7000 schedule, lease schedule and depreciation schedule, and DESE’s desk-review or audit findings on them.
comparisonHow is a regional school district’s assessment apportioned between its member towns, and what does each town actually appropriate for schools?NARROWED 26 September 2026. This used to say a regional town could not be compared at all. That was asking at the wrong level: Chapter 70 is computed per MUNICIPALITY whatever district its children attend, so DESE publishes, for all 351 towns, the foundation budget for that town’s own children, the contribution the town is REQUIRED to make and by subtraction what the state adds — Ashby is required to raise $7,819 per child, Groton $10,748, Lunenburg $8,571. What is still unpublished is the step between: how the district divides its assessment among members, and what each member town actually appropriates, which may be well above the required minimum. — closes: each regional district’s annual assessment schedule, voted by its member towns’ meetings and filed with DESE.
comparisonWhat are the current teacher salary schedules in Groton-Dunstable, Ayer Shirley, Leominster and Ashburnham-Westminster?NARROWED 19 October 2026. The current agreements of Lunenburg, Harvard, North Middlesex, Fitchburg and Montachusett are held and their salary schedules read cell by cell (sources/data/teacher-salary-schedules.csv); on those five FY2026 schedules Lunenburg’s bachelor’s and master’s top steps are the lowest, before longevity, which every contract but Harvard’s pays outside the grid. For these four districts the only contracts held are the ones DESE publishes, and each has expired: Groton-Dunstable’s schedules run 2017-18 to 2019-20, Ayer Shirley’s 2019-20 to 2021-22, Leominster’s 2015-16 to 2017-18 and Ashburnham-Westminster’s 2016-17 to 2018-19. So three of the project’s six comparison districts cannot be compared on pay scale for any current year. See /school-spending-history/teacher-pay-compared. — closes: each district’s current Unit A teachers’ agreement, with its salary schedules, by records request.
comparisonWhich towns does Lunenburg consider comparable to itself, for tax and budget purposes?This project compares Lunenburg with five peer towns and that set is OURS. Nothing the town has published names a cohort: a 2023 Finance Committee minute cites "the 8 communities that were surveyed" for a salary study and never lists them, and no budget document, capital plan or assessors’ report names a comparison group. So every "compared with similar towns" statement on either side rests on a set nobody has agreed. — closes: the eight-community list behind the 2023 salary survey, which the Town Administrator or the bargaining unit that commissioned it holds.
curriculumHow many classes ran in each subject at Lunenburg Middle School and Lunenburg High before SY2017Every trend on /what-courses-actually-ran is read inside an era, because for four years — SY2013 to SY2016 — Thomas C Passios was closed and every remaining school held one grade band higher, with grade 8 in the high school building. Four subjects move by more than ten points of participation into those years and back out of them without anything changing about what a ninth to twelfth grader was offered. So the file cannot say what the schools as they are now offered before SY2017 — the schools as they are now did not exist. — closes: nothing published can. DESE files by school and the schools changed; the question is only answerable by grade, and the state’s class-size collection carries no grade inside a school.
curriculumHow many classes ran in each subject at the two elementary schoolsThe counts swing by a factor of two between adjacent years with no matching change in enrolment, and two school-years report an average class size no primary school can have — 87.1 at Lunenburg Primary in SY2011 and 36.5 in SY2022, against a maximum of 24.1 everywhere else. The subject coding of a self-contained classroom is not stable enough to trend, so the elementary half of the district cannot be read at all. — closes: DESE’s Student Course Schedule submission detail for Lunenburg, which carries the course records behind the published aggregate.
curriculumWhat is taught in the fifth of Lunenburg High sections DESE files as Miscellaneous51 of the high school’s 247 sections in SY2025, averaging 4.9 students, in a subject area DESE gives no course names for — and the single largest mover in the section count since SY2017. The only public account of one is a student describing a new elective with four on the register and eight on the first day. — closes: The LHS master schedule by year, or the district’s own Student Course Schedule submission to DESE, which holds the course records the published aggregate is built from.
curriculumWhich courses a Lunenburg High student could actually choose from, in any yearDESE publishes sections by SUBJECT AREA and never by course, so an elective ending is invisible inside a subject total that rose — a student told the School Committee on 7 February 2024 that Music Tech would be "non-existent", and the high school's Arts sections went from 24 that year to 25 the next. Both statements are true and this archive cannot hold them together. — closes: The district’s own Program of Studies for each year, which the High School Principal handed the School Committee on 6 March 2024, and the LHS master schedule presented to the School Committee on 4 December 2024. Neither is published.
curriculumWhy fewer Lunenburg High students take a history or a language course than before SY2020Three DESE series move together for both subjects — teacher FTE, student places and the share of the school taking one — and the fall in each begins in the years the school closed and reopened. A staffing decision, a change in what the timetable allowed, and students choosing differently all fit the same three numbers, and the state files nothing that separates them. — closes: the district’s course-request tallies for each year — what students asked for beside what ran. The High School Principal told the School Committee on 6 March 2024 that courses are whittled away once student choices are entered, so the tally exists at the moment the decision is made and is not published.
document_wantedDESE End of Year Financial ReportNARROWED 5 October 2026. the Finance Committee files received by records request on 4 October 2026 (sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/, see its PROVENANCE note) include the district's FY2023 and FY2024 End of Year Financial Report WORKBOOKS (eoy23 and eoy24, district 162, Schedules 1, 3, 18, 19 and 20), which separate spending by fund. Both are working copies passed on from a Select Board member's records request, not the reports as filed: the FY24 grant columns do not match DESE's published file. The filed reports remain the remedy. Published by the state. — closes: Separates district spending by FUND, which is the one thing the town’s budget documents never show.
document_wantedDESE's competitive award lists before FY2026DESE's Grant Allocations & Awards page links competitive award lists for FY2026 and the current year only; fy25-awards.html, fy24- and fy23- redirect to its 404 page (checked 23 October 2026). So who won a competitive grant before FY2026 cannot be compared. — closes: DESE's competitive award lists for FY2023 to FY2025, by records request
document_wantedHow the Montachusett regional agreement apportions costs among its member townsThe apportionment method is now on the record twice: the district printed it in Lunenburg’s FY2017 annual town report — four parts, with transportation and other operating divided by each town’s 1 October enrollment share and capital divided by each town’s school-attending children in grades 1 to 12 — and DESE’s own apportionment sheet, reprinted in the FY2027 budget presentation, shows the required-contribution part split between a town’s two districts by foundation-budget share. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS THE INSTRUMENT. A budget book states current practice; the regional agreement is what binds it, and it is the document that would say whether the ratios can be changed, how bonds are apportioned and over what term, what a member town’s withdrawal would require, and what amendments have been made. Asked at the Finance Committee on 5 February 2026 whether the agreement was indefinite or could be renegotiated, the Superintendent-Director said he believed it was ongoing and that amendments were very rare. A recollection at a meeting is not the instrument. — closes: the Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School District regional agreement and its amendments, filed with the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education and held by the district and by each member town’s clerk.
document_wantedThe Cherry Sheet itself — what the state told Lunenburg to expect, receipt by receiptThis archive holds no Cherry Sheet for any year. The Cherry Sheet is the state’s own statement of estimated aid and assessments to a Massachusetts town, and it is what a tax rate is set on. Without it the only measurement of aid estimate error this project can make is one net line on the Division of Local Services free cash proof — Excess/Shortfall Cherry Sheet Receipts (CL#8) — which lumps Chapter 70, Unrestricted General Government Aid, the abatement reimbursements and every other receipt into a single figure. So a year that came in $390,814 short can be reported as short and cannot be reported as short in anything. — closes: DLS Cherry Sheet CS 1-ER (estimated receipts) and CS 1-EB (estimated charges) for Lunenburg, FY2021 to FY2027.
document_wantedThe Town Manager’s revenue apportionment worksheetSeen once; we do not hold it. — closes: Documents the convention by which general-fund revenue is presented as split across departments. It cannot make the edge traceable — nothing can — but it makes the convention citable.
document_wantedThe period 13 ledgerThe year-end close. — closes: Reconciles FY2026 properly; period 12 is used for now.
document_wantedThe town’s Chapter 32B enrollment scheduleNARROWED 5 October 2026. The Finance Committee's general fund history (FY2010-FY2025, sources/data/gl-history.csv) carries a separate SCHOOL RETIREES health insurance line in the town's budget in every year FY2022-FY2025, original budget 1,149,925 rising to 1,411,181 -- so the RETIREE split is printed in four years, not two. The split of active employees' insurance between town and schools is still not printed. Not published anywhere in this archive; the town must hold one to administer the plan and set premium shares. — closes: Splits every insurance account between the town and the schools, in every year, instead of in the two years the split happens to be printed.
document_wantedWRRS annual actuarial valuation, by member unitPublished by the retirement system. — closes: Sizes the school share of the $2.39M pension assessment.
document_wantedWhat school spending has been in constant dollarsCLOSED 18 October 2026. The Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI-U for Boston-Cambridge-Newton (series CUURS11ASA0, January 1990 onward) is landed in sources/federal-bls/, four API responses saved as returned with their addresses and sha256, and its PROVENANCE.md says how the fiscal-year average is built. Every spending page on /school-spending-history now gives dollars as printed beside dollars of the latest actual year, July-June averages, our arithmetic. What the index does NOT settle: it measures what a basket of consumer goods costs in the Boston area, not what a school pays for teachers, tuition or insurance, so "after prices" means after general prices -- closes: the CPI-U for Boston-Cambridge-Newton, landed; for a school-specific measure, the state and local government price deflator the state uses to inflate the Chapter 70 foundation budget.
document_wantedWhere bus fee receipts are bookedA revenue account, a fund, or a statement that they are netted before booking. — closes: The fee schedule is published and verified; STUDENTBUS shows zero. A charged fee with no observable destination is the clearest single gap in this model.
document_wantedWhich TABLE in a document is ledger-backed, rather than which document isdocument-basis.csv carries one basis per document — 322 paths, 322 rows — and that granularity is wrong for the annual town reports, which are the source of a great deal of what this project publishes. The FY2022 annual town report is classified forward, and it contains both 'Combined balance sheet, all fund types and account groups, 30 June 2022' and 'FY 2023 Omnibus Budget (as voted)'. A closing statement prepared by the Town Accountant and next year's budget, in one PDF, under one label. All twelve annual town reports carry forward, which would make the special revenue schedule and the combined balance sheet look like budget documents when each ties to its own printed totals every year. Nothing published rests on this being wrong, because those datasets are validated by their own control totals rather than by the basis label — but the column cannot be used to answer 'is this figure ledger-backed', which is what it looks like it answers. — closes: nothing external. This is ours to fix: a basis per table family in annual_report_catalogue, set where the reconciliation is already known, rather than one per document in document-basis.csv.
document_wantedglytdbud-expense for the special revenue fundsNARROWED 5 October 2026 for the SCHOOL funds in FY2024. the Finance Committee files received by records request on 4 October 2026 (sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/, see its PROVENANCE note) include the school department's FY2024 period 13 glytdbud report covering every school fund, grants and revolving funds included, at org and object level. The town's own special revenue funds are not in it. The identical report the town already runs for the general fund and for each of the four enterprise funds, pointed at funds 13xx/22xx/26xx–29xx instead. — closes: Turns every restricted edge above from presumption into traced fact — athletics, lunch, circuit breaker, extended day, and every grant.
extractionCan we trust gross wages, name by name enough to chart what the town pays its people in total?7,644 of 11,446 rows in report_gross_wages are reconciled to a total the document itself prints — 255 failed that check and 3,547 were never checked. The figures are read and published, so a query returns them and they look confident; only the status column says otherwise. Every page was surveyed before anyone tried: of 16 years, 6 need real PDF geometry rather than text, 9 are messy and 1 are clean — mirrored layouts, rows offset from their own names, a missing fund-name column, and column counts that change between years. NO year of this family prints a grand total, so there is no arithmetic on the page to foot a row against and no extractor can supply one. — closes: nothing we can build. What stands in for a total here is the PAIRING and the order the list prints itself in, both of which prove the assignment and say nothing about the digits; a reconcilable figure needs a total from the Town. The per-year survey is in sources/data/extraction-plan.csv.

extractionHow many financial pages do the annual town reports actually contain?The page tracker's universe is built from what RECOGNITION found: a page is listed only if fifteen money figures were recognised on it. FY2024 page 189 prints ninety-six wages and recognition found ZERO, so it was not unfinished, it was ABSENT -- and five of the eight pages of that wage run were. FY2024 was reported as 22 financial pages and is at least 28. A page a person has now read is added to the map, so the eight are on it; nothing finds the pages nobody has looked at yet, and the same failure is unmeasured in the other fifteen reports. A screen for candidates -- many boxes, almost no recognised money -- returns about 1,800 pages archive-wide, but it catches every page of ordinary prose too and is a finding aid rather than a count. — closes: nothing from the Town. Every page is already held; what is missing is somebody looking at the ones recognition could not read.
extractionRESOLVED 2 October 2026 — PDF page 51 of the FY2019 debt schedule was never absent from the tracker, and it is now readCLOSED, AND BOTH HALVES OF THE ORIGINAL CLAIM WERE WRONG. The tracker held 2019,51,debt,3,unread,... — the page was unread, not absent, so this row was a statement about our reading of the tracker rather than about the archive (learning-loop entry 12). And it is not "the missing middle": p51 carries the TOTAL column every issue is proved against, plus the second half of the fiscal years. Its figures=50 was a RECOGNITION count, low by 2.7x — the page prints 136. All four pages (49-52) were read off their own JPEG2000 bitmaps at 150 dpi on 2 October 2026: 879 figures, 34 files, 17 groups, four nested identities, and the printed corner closing on itself exactly — 46,568,549 + 18,922,925 = 65,491,474 and + 25,861 = 65,517,335. — closes: nothing further; the question was ours and it is answered.
extractionWhat cash did the Treasurer hold in the years whose column does not foot to the page’s own printed total?1 page of the Treasurer’s cash on hand in the annual town reports is READ AND REFUSED: an extractor reached it, could not tie the rows to a total the page itself prints, and published nothing. So a query about the Treasurer’s cash on hand returns silence for FY2019, and the silence is ours rather than the town’s — every one of these pages IS printed. Refusals and their reasons are in sources/data/extraction-blocked.csv; the pages are listed in sources/data/annual-report-pages.csv where state is refused. Re-running a model over them returns the same refusal and pays for it. — closes: the column ruler in the treasurer’s-cash reader; the page prints the total the column must reach, and sources/data/extraction-blocked.csv records both figures.
extractionWhat did the Town have receivable at 30 June 2020, line by line, across all three pages of the summary?receivables.csv holds 43 rows for FY2020 -- 31 on annual-report page 47, 12 on page 48 and NONE on page 49 -- while receivables-reconciliation.csv records the same run as 87 rows and says it ties to its printed GRAND TOTAL on all eight columns. Page 47 alone prints about 44 rows. Page 49 was read by eye on 2 October 2026 and all eleven of its rows (ten detail plus the run's GRAND TOTAL) close on the identity the page states, so the page is readable and the extractor's refusal -- no single sign convention proves the page (2 of 5 rows at best) -- is a statement about the instrument. Summing the 43 published rows plus the ten read from page 49 gives $375,657.49 forward against a printed GRAND TOTAL of $9,108,033.04, so the published extract is short of what the pages print by most of the table. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: whether the missing rows were dropped by the reader or were never published -- nobody has read pages 47 and 48 by eye. -- closes: nothing from the Town is needed. The remedy is ours: read pages 47 and 48 of the FY2020 annual town report the way page 49 was read, and foot all three pages to the printed GRAND TOTAL.
extractionWhat did the town owe on each bond issue, principal and interest, in the years whose repayment schedule cannot be read?1 page of the debt repayment schedule in the annual town reports is READ AND REFUSED: an extractor reached it, could not tie the rows to a total the page itself prints, and published nothing. So a query about the debt repayment schedule returns silence for FY2011, and the silence is ours rather than the town’s — every one of these pages IS printed. Refusals and their reasons are in sources/data/debt-repayment-detail-refused.csv; the pages are listed in sources/data/annual-report-pages.csv where state is refused. Re-running a model over them returns the same refusal and pays for it. — closes: a reader of scripts/extract_debt_tables.py measuring the year header and splitting the merged year boxes by the pitch the page itself sets, then publishing only the columns where PRINCIPAL + INTEREST foots to the printed TOTAL for that issue.
extractionWhat did the town pay its people, name by name, in the years whose payroll listing produced nothing?1 page of gross wages, name by name in the annual town reports is READ AND REFUSED: an extractor reached it, could not tie the rows to a total the page itself prints, and published nothing. So a query about gross wages, name by name returns silence for FY2012, and the silence is ours rather than the town’s — every one of these pages IS printed. Refusals and their reasons are in sources/data/gross-wages-refused.csv; the pages are listed in sources/data/annual-report-pages.csv where state is refused. Re-running a model over them returns the same refusal and pays for it. — closes: a Vision RE-READ of the page, which is free and is what closed FY2019: its seven pages held 871 boxes in our cache against 1,753 on a re-read, and two of them held the surname column and no money at all. The refusals that survive a re-read are scan defects rather than layout — FY2019 p200 loses a 21-row band that produced no box at scale 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8 — and those close only with a better copy of the page from the Town. Note that the town stopped printing the department beside each name after FY2016, so these pages bound the question rather than settling it.
extractionWhat did the town receive in FY2023, receipt line by receipt line?The FY2023 receipts page -- annual report page 25 -- cannot be read. It is a photograph embedded at 93 dpi, and it packs about 150 line items across three column-pairs of a landscape page, so the digits are below the resolution of the stored image: 588 and 568, 405 and 465, 009 and 000 are not distinguishable at any magnification, because the detail is not in the file to magnify. Reading the SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS block gives a total $20 from the printed GRAND TOTAL of $45,549,438.56, consistent with exactly one misread digit, and choosing the digit that makes it close would be fitting the answer to the check. For contrast the same report stores page 50 at 183 dpi and page 53 at 156 dpi, and both are legible. RE-CHECKED 1 October 2026 off the page's own embedded bitmap rather than off the recognition cache, with the grid measured by projection and the amount columns rendered at 20x: the labels are legible and the figures are not, so what the town received money FOR in FY2023 is readable and how much is not. And a better scan is not a remedy that exists. Of the two publisher addresses on record, DocumentCenter/View/4131 now returns HTTP 404 and ArchiveCenter/ViewFile/Item/160 returns 18,274,143 bytes -- byte-for-byte the copy this archive already holds. — closes: the Treasurer's own FY2023 receipts file, or a MUNIS revenue report for FY2023; this archive holds neither, and no MUNIS revenue export for any year.
extractionWhat does each individual debt issue cost the town in a given year, and which of them fall off when?FY2022 NO LONGER BELONGS TO THIS GAP: its schedule was read by issue on 29 September 2026 -- 14 borrowings against 25 fiscal years, 184 issue-years, each closing on its own printed TOTAL row and reconciling to the GRAND TOTAL block on pages 46 and 48. The FY2023 AND FY2024 annual reports' debt repayment schedules each print about fifty debt issues against twenty-three fiscal years, roughly 1,200 figures, and only its GRAND TOTAL block has been read: principal, interest, principal and interest, MWPAT admin fees and total debt, FY2025 to FY2047, which foot to the schedule's own TOTAL column. So the town's debt SERVICE by year is established and the COMPOSITION of it is not — a resident cannot see which bond ends in which year, or what the Meadow Woods water general obligation costs on its own. — closes: nothing further is needed from the Town. The figures are printed on page 53 of the FY2023 report and page 37 of the FY2024 report and have simply not been transcribed.
extractionWhat is on the calendar-edition pages that were read and deliberately not landed?13 pages of pages of the 2001-2010 reports read by eye and not landed in the annual town reports are READ AND REFUSED: an extractor reached them, could not tie the rows to a total the page itself prints, and published nothing. So a query about pages of the 2001-2010 reports read by eye and not landed returns silence for FY1973, FY1975, FY1977, FY1984, FY1985, FY1988, FY1995, FY2006, and the silence is ours rather than the town’s — every one of these pages IS printed. Refusals and their reasons are in sources/data/read_report_tables.csv; the pages are listed in sources/data/annual-report-pages.csv where state is refused. Re-running a model over them returns the same refusal and pays for it. — closes: the reason in that edition’s map.csv and the item in its NEEDS.md: a re-read of a page printed rotated, or an emitter for a layout the reader cannot yet express.

Refusals and their reasons are in sources/data/read-and-refused.csv; the pages are listed in sources/data/annual-report-pages.csv where state is refused. extractionWhat was the town owed, account by account, in the years whose receivables page will not foot?3 pages of what is owed to the town in the annual town reports are READ AND REFUSED: an extractor reached them, could not tie the rows to a total the page itself prints, and published nothing. So a query about what is owed to the town returns silence for FY2013, FY2017, FY2020, and the silence is ours rather than the town’s — every one of these pages IS printed.
