Searched for capital plan, capital project, capital outlay and capital expend on all 70 pages (sources/data/report-tables/1994/). — closes: the FY95 Capital Plan as presented to the May 14, 1994 Annual Town Meeting.
money_outWhat service period do FLLAC invoices 27L2KEY11-19 bill for?Their numbers, their rate ($19,885.50 against FY2026's $19,255.50) and their timing all point to the first quarter of FY2027, but the journal records no service dates, and the numbering is our reading of FLLAC's. If they bill FY2027, FY2026's surplus reads $189,277 smaller than what FY2026 needed for FY2026. — closes: FLLAC's invoices 27L2KEY11 to 27L2KEY19, with their service dates.
money_outWhat share of the schools’ grounds, custodial, heating and utility cost is athleticsThe town’s ledger codes every school account to a function, and athletics is function 3510 — 12 accounts, $518,334 appropriated in FY2026, which ties to the cent to the district’s own budget book. Custodians, heating, utilities, grounds and building maintenance are separate functions in the same printout, $2,035,523 revised across the whole school department in FY2026, and not one of those accounts carries the athletics program segment. The fields are mown, the gym is lit and heated and the lines are painted, so some of that $2,035,523 is a cost of school sports — but nothing published splits it out, no document states an allocation, and the athletics revolving fund’s cashbook does not name a field, a light or a custodian on any of its 277 postings. So every published athletics total, including this project’s, is a floor and not a total. — closes: a cost allocation from the district or the Town Accountant apportioning functions 4110, 4120, 4130, 4210 and 4220 across the programmes that use the buildings and grounds; failing that, the accounts-payable detail behind the grounds-maintenance warrants, which would at least name what was mown, lined or resurfaced and when.
money_outWhat the Dee Bus rates and fleet were in FY2025, so the 7.6% FY2026 increase can be split into price and busesThe FY2026 budget's "7.6% line increase = $69,300" is exactly the new contract's first-year regular-route price ($976,500: 8 buses at $485 and 3 at $515 a day, 180 days) over the FY2025 budget line ($907,200). The new contract fixes every year's price per bus per day, so FY2027 and FY2028 are known; the FY2025 side is one number, $907,200, which fits eleven buses at an average $458.18 a day (all of the 7.6% is price) and ten at $504.00 (the increase is a bus, not price) equally well. A district presentation says 11 buses were in use; that is a statement, not a rate. Requested on 9 October 2026 and not delivered. See notes/findings/DEE-BUS-CONTRACT.md. — closes: the FY2023-FY2025 Dee Bus contract and its bid form (daily price per bus by size, number of buses), or the FY2025 Dee Bus invoices.
money_outWhat the PEG Access fund spent in FY2020 and in FY2024In both years the annual town report prints two totals for the same year's PEG expenses and they differ. FY2020, both tables on printed page 75: FY20 Line Item Expenses by Percentage foots to Total $116,933.22 and FY20 REVENUE vs EXPENSES prints Expenses $116,933.54 -- 32 cents apart. FY2024: the statement on printed page 63 prints Expenses $174,150 and the line-item table on printed page 64 foots to Total $174,151.16, and since that statement is printed in whole dollars throughout, rounding 174,151.16 gives 174,151 rather than 174,150. Each table foots to its own printed total exactly, so neither is internally wrong; they disagree with each other. FY2017 is a third case of the same shape: its ten printed expense lines add to $74,665.74 against a printed TOTAL of $74,215.73, a difference of $450.01, of which $450.00 is the Vendor Expenses line that the facing pie chart also omits. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: which figure is the year's expenditure in any of the three years. -- closes: the MUNIS year-to-date expense report (glytdbud) for the PEG Access and Cable Related Enterprise Fund for FY2017, FY2020 and FY2024, the same report the town already runs for the general fund.
money_outWhat the athletic fee fund’s high school purchase-of-service account paid for in FY2026Account 1301-3-300-3510-06-0-00-2-531006, where athletic buses were charged before they moved to the general fund, books officials, ice time, dues and transportation together. money_outWhat the four ADJ EXP journal entries moved, and from where$254,121.18 — 65% of everything that reached the athletics revolving fund in FY2025 — arrived on four general-journal entries whose entire description is an expense adjustment made per a memo. An entry raising cash in a fund and labelled as an expense adjustment fits at least three readings: expenses charged here and later moved elsewhere, a transfer in from another fund, or a correction of charges posted to the wrong account. Those are different facts about the world and identical facts on the page, and the same shape of entry could be adjusting any fund in the town without either budget document showing a trace. — closes: the five memos the ledger names, dated 08/12/24, 01/30/25, 05/02/25, 07/02/25 and 08/20/2025.
money_outWhat the money was that reached departments’ revised budgets outside any recorded transferIn the general fund history the revised budget differs from original plus transfers in and out on about one account-year in twenty, almost always upward, in every year FY2010–FY2025, and the workbook’s own Grand Total shows the same gap. By dollars, most of it is no larger than what the same account left unspent the year before, which is what a carried-forward encumbrance would look like; the rest fits a supplemental appropriation at a special Town Meeting. Neither is confirmed, and the difference matters: a carry-forward is last year’s money, a supplemental appropriation is new money. Measured in /analysis/department-budgets. — closes: the MUNIS budget amendment detail for each fiscal year, or the Town Accountant’s appropriations schedule with its APPROPRIATED FORWARD column, which the annual report printed through FY2023.
money_outWhat the schools actually spent, per line, in any year before FY2026NARROWED 5 October 2026. the Finance Committee files received by records request on 4 October 2026 (sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/, see its PROVENANCE note) include the school department's FY2024 MUNIS year-to-date report at PERIOD 13 (glytdbud, FOR 2024 13, generated 08/07/2024, every school fund), which answers FY2024 by ledger, and a general fund budget-vs-actual history, FY2010-FY2025 by account, assembled from MUNIS into one workbook. FY2025 in that workbook is part-year. The district publishes a column headed ACTUAL in its forward budget books, and twelve years of it load as budget_figure where stage='restated' — the stage was called actual until 7 September 2026, and the rename is the point. Those are RESTATEMENTS — a prior year re-presented inside a document written by the party that spent it — and document-basis.csv classifies all sixteen source documents behind them as restatement (14) or forward (2). None is a ledger. The archive holds ten ledger documents in total, and the only ones reaching school general-fund spending are one quarter of FY23 and FY2026 period 12. So the question 'did the schools spend what they budgeted' cannot be settled before FY2026 from anything published: both sides of the comparison come out of the same budget book, and a restatement cannot show money moved between lines mid-year because approved transfers do not appear in a budget document. — closes: the MUNIS year-end expense report (glytdbud, period 13) for the school department for each year wanted, which is the same report we already hold for FY2026.

money_outWhere did each FY2026 school line-item transfer come from, and where did it go?The MUNIS year-to-date report gives one NET transfer figure per account, so a line that gave and received money in the same year shows only the difference. The 29 July 2026 School Committee minutes record $11,000 moved out of natural-gas heating; the ledger shows heating up $11,024.22, net. The 5 November 2025 minutes record $13,500 moved to School Committee dues "to cover superintendent search invoice"; that line closed FY2026 with $13,689 unspent and had spent less than its original budget. /analysis/fy26-school-surplus — closes: the MUNIS budget transfer report for department 300, FY2026, gross, with each entry's date and counterparty account.
money_outWhere did the $122,502.44 that moved out of the FY2025 school department mid-year go, and what posted to department 300 after the School Committee's 17 September 2025 surplus statement?The closed MUNIS ledger (sources/data/munis-school-ytd.csv, FY2025 period 13, department 300) carries transfers_adjustments as a net figure per account, with no counterparty -- so a line moved in cannot be matched to the line it moved out of. And the ledger's own $627,116.86 available at the close exceeds the $603,885.97 the district reported that day by $23,230.89, with no single account or pair of accounts equal to the gap, which is consistent with activity posted after 17 September 2025 but not established by anything held here. — closes: the FY2025 transfer schedule for department 300 with counterparties and authority, and the journal entries posted to department 300 after 17 September 2025.
money_outWhere was the schools’ FY2024 employee insurance reported, if not in the school department’s End of Year Financial Report?NARROWED 5 October 2026, and possibly reframed. the Finance Committee files received by records request on 4 October 2026 (sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/, see its PROVENANCE note) include a general fund budget-vs-actual history that carries the school department's active health insurance inside the SCHOOL general fund in every year FY2010-FY2025: account 0100-3-300-5200-99-1-99-2-570001, FY2024 actual 3,212,078.37 (sheet School Only, row 396). A Budget Master note records '$1,522,236 SHIFTED TO SCHOOL DEPT.' at FY2003 to FY2004. Why the EOYR total differs is not established. DESE’s EOYR shows function 5200 Insurance for Active Employees at $485,010 in FY2024 against $3,286,872 in FY2023 and $3,511,566 in FY2025; a difference read across that year looks like a $3M rise and is a reporting gap closing. Whether the year was mis-filed or the town appropriated and reported the insurance outside the school department is not established. — closes: the district’s FY2024 EOYR as submitted, Schedule 1, and the town’s FY2024 appropriation for group insurance by department.
money_outWhether Lunenburg spends the foundation budget the way the state assumes it will, category by categoryChapter 70 builds its foundation budget from about eleven CATEGORIES — classroom teachers, administration, instructional leadership, materials, and so on — each with a per-pupil rate the state sets. That is the state saying what an adequate education costs and how it decomposes. Comparing it line for line against what the district actually spends on the same categories would show exactly where Lunenburg is above and below the state’s own model, and it is the single most useful unanswered question about the expense side. WE HOLD THE TOTAL AND NOT THE PARTS. dese-ch70-foundation-nss.xlsx carries required net school spending, actual net school spending and the foundation budget as single figures per district per year, and dese-ch70-key-factors.xlsx carries the aid calculation; neither breaks the foundation budget into its categories. So the comparison cannot be made from this archive at all, in any year. WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE INSTEAD: dividing the foundation total by DESE’s statewide category shares to estimate Lunenburg’s. That produces a number for every category and establishes nothing, because the shares are what the comparison is meant to test. — closes: DESE’s foundation budget detail workbook, which prints the per-pupil rates and the resulting category amounts for every district, published annually beside the Chapter 70 aid figures this project already holds.
money_outWhether a general fund athletics line is net of the revolving fundIn FY2024 the town’s comparable athletics lines came to $124,301 against $351,643 the district’s own sport-by-sport workbook totals for the same categories — so the appropriation covered 35% of the cost. That is measurable for FY2024 and FY2025 only, because those are the only years anybody published both halves. For every other year, and every other programme, a line that rose because the cost rose looks exactly like a line that rose because a fund stopped paying part of it. — closes: the MUNIS Account_Detail export for the general fund athletics orgs S3066672 and S3066671, all object codes.
money_outWhether a general fund rise beside a grant fall is the same cost, or a different cost in the same functionDESE's End of Year Financial Report splits every function code into general fund and grants/revolving, so a function where grants fell and the general fund rose in the same year can be MEASURED — 8 of them in Lunenburg in SY2025, grants -$1,127,647 against general fund +$1,136,013 (dese_function_expenditure). Sorting those functions into “swapped” and “reduced” is OUR label on the signs of two numbers, and the state publishes no such classification. A function code is a bucket: Teachers, Classroom covers every classroom teacher in four schools, and both funds can move inside it for reasons that have nothing to do with each other. So the split establishes that the funding mix moved and cannot establish that the town picked up the thing the grant was paying for. — closes: the district's grant award letters and end-of-grant expenditure reports, naming the posts and object codes each grant paid, set against the general fund payroll and object detail for the same function in the following year.
money_outWhether a school line that stops appearing in the district’s book stopped being fundedA line can leave the book because the money stopped, or because the book changed shape. Both look identical: an absence. Between FY2022 and FY2023 the restated series moves from one district budget book to another, the number of printed lines falls by about a third, and the reported total RISES — so the lines that stop appearing at that boundary cannot have taken their money with them. At least five of the disappearances are established renames, two lines differing only in spelling and carrying the identical value in every year they share (Maint. of Buildings/Contrcted Services and Maint. of Buildings/Contracted Services). Nothing published maps the older line list onto the newer one, so for any individual line, absence is a fact about the document and not about the service. — closes: the district’s own crosswalk from the FY2022 budget-book line list to the FY2023 presentation, or the MUNIS year-end expense report (glytdbud, period 13) for the school department for those years, which is keyed on accounts rather than on printed line names.
money_outWhether a town department’s budget growth is more service or a cost moved into it from another budgetSeveral town departments’ starting budgets grew in single steps — general highway maintenance, facilities and grounds, public buildings and recycling each have one year in which the starting budget rose by more than a third — and a step that size fits a service being taken on, or a cost moved in from another line or fund, as well as it fits the same service costing more. The ledger records dollars by account and nothing about why an account moved, so a growth rate measured across such a step is not a trend. Measured in /analysis/department-budgets. — closes: the Town Manager’s budget message, or the Finance Committee’s report to Town Meeting, for each year in which a department’s starting budget stepped.
money_outWhether spending less per pupil is a choice or a constraintLunenburg’s total per-pupil spending has been below the statewide first quartile in every one of the seventeen years DESE publishes, and its net school spending is a smaller multiple of the required minimum than the median district’s. Nothing in any of these documents distinguishes a town that decided to spend less from a town that could not raise more: the levy limit, two failed overrides, the district’s proposed budget and Town Meeting’s vote all resolve into the same single number, and the number is the outcome of all of them at once. This matters because the two readings imply opposite remedies. — closes: nothing published settles it; the nearest evidence is the district’s own level-service request against the appropriation voted, year by year, which the archive holds for FY2024 onward only.
money_outWhether the FY2025 spring section of the district’s by-sport athletics workbook is completeThe district's sport-by-sport workbook prints $0.00 as its FY2025 spring season total, in cell AT25, while its spring rows sum to $18,242.50, 46.1% below FY2024's spring rows; spring is 58.9% of the whole fall in athletic transportation from FY2024 to FY2025. Outdoor track, baseball, softball and lacrosse all look cheaper in FY2025 on that sheet, and /analysis/transportation cannot say whether that is fewer or shorter trips or a section filled in before the season's bills arrived. Every other season total the workbook prints equals its own rows. — closes: the district's confirmation that the FY2025 spring transportation column is final, or Dee Bus's spring 2025 athletic invoices, from the Business Office.
money_outWhether the school committee sets the special education budget expecting the circuit breaker and grants to pay the restMEASURED (/special-education/sped-all-funds): on the accounts the ledger labels special education, the general fund came in under its voted budget in three of the four years FY2023-FY2026 and ran over in FY2026 (spent counting what was still owed at year end), and the circuit breaker and grants paid more on top -- so total special education spending passed the vote every year. SETTLED FOR ONE PART: the circuit breaker on collaborative tuition. The FY2025 and FY2026 approved books print a circuit breaker offset under that line, the voted figure is the line less the offset, and the FY2025 ledger loads the line gross and cuts it by the offset on 1 July (/school-all-funds/fy-breakdown, the plan against what happened). The FY2023 and FY2024 books print no offset. STILL OPEN: no book prints any grant offset, so whether the vote counted on grants, or on the circuit breaker for any other line, is intent no document held records. — closes: the district's special education budget build for each year, with the circuit breaker and grant offsets it assumed.
money_outWhether the schools’ stated field and grounds costs match the books — about $126,000 of grounds work in FY2024 and $38,100 of outsourced mowing and field repair, paid, the Superintendent says, from the same revolving fund the field rent goes intoThe figures are the district’s own, read back from FY24 budget requests in an email of September 2026, and nothing in the archive tests them: fund 1306’s FY2024 expenditure is not published and the fund’s journal is not held — closes: the journal detail for fund 1306, FY2024–FY2026, and the FY2024 and FY2025 special-revenue reports.
money_outWhich accounts Lunenburg's FY2025 health insurance figure on the state's Schedule A countsThe state's figure for Lunenburg equals the town insurance department less Medicare and life insurance in every year FY2010-FY2023, and the whole department in FY2024 (asserted in scripts/build_health_insurance_topics.py). So any growth rate measured across FY2024 mixes a change in what was counted with a change in spending, and FY2025 cannot be tied because the ledger history's FY2025 actuals are part-year. — closes: the town's FY2025 Schedule A health insurance detail, set against the year-end ledger.
money_outWhich budget line each dollar of grant and revolving money paid forThe fund split now exists at DESE's function level and nowhere below it. Lunenburg SY2025 spent $3,044,898 of grants and revolving money against $26,986,344 of general fund across all functions. But the district's budget book prints one NET figure per printed line (rule 11), DESE prints one figure per function code, and no published document maps the second onto the first — so a line that rose because a grant ended still looks identical to a line that rose because the district grew. This is the budget-line half of Which fund pays which post, which is the same wall approached from the staffing side. — closes: DESE's End of Year Financial Report Schedule 1 as Lunenburg files it, which separates revenues and expenditures by source of funds; or the MUNIS year-to-date expense report run for the school grant and revolving funds rather than the general fund.
money_outWhich budget lines the School Committee's line item transfers moved, when the minutes record only the voteOf the transfers the School Committee approved in the minutes read so far (every set the archive holds, 6 September 2023 to 26 August 2026), some are recorded only as a vote to approve transfers "as outlined" or "as presented", or as one total for a batch, with no from-line, to-line or amount -- 24 June 2026 approved four transfers with no figure printed, and 4 October 2023 approved $127,786 as a single total. The minutes are the record of the VOTE; the lines are on the district's transfer sheet the committee is shown, and the archive holds that sheet for only three: 26 September 2025 (the athletic $20,000), 5-6 October 2026 (FY2027) and one from October 2022. The recordings cannot substitute: a caption model hears figures unreliably. And the town's ledger extracts held here carry no budget-transfer journal for the school department, so nothing can tie a vote to the accounts it moved. — closes: the line item transfer sheets presented at each School Committee meeting (in the meeting packets), or the MUNIS budget transfer journal for the school department, by fiscal year.
money_outWhich department carried forward the $362.00 the FY2017 appropriations schedule does not print?The FY2017 GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS schedule, pages 24-28 of the annual town report, states twice that a $362.00 carry-forward exists and never prints the line. Its APPROPRIATED FORWARD column sums to $37,626,083.44 against a printed GRAND TOTAL of $37,626,445.44, and its footer legend fwd - forward from FY 2016 $637,981.43 exceeds the 26 fwd lines actually printed by the same $362.00 — while the srt and rft legend totals reproduce to the cent and the other three columns tie exactly. The subtotal for Police Fire Medical Expenses on page 25 is $5,362.00 over a single line item of $5,000.00, so the money belongs to that block; which prior-year appropriation it is a carry-forward OF is not stated anywhere in the document. The amount is trivial; the question is not, because the same schedule is the basis of every departmental growth rate this project measures and a carry-forward line changes which year a dollar belongs to. — closes: the Town Accountant's FY2017 year-end MUNIS encumbrance and carry-forward detail, which lists each forwarded balance by account.
money_outWhich earlier school account a new account continues, when a line is renumbered or splitThe school journal matches a line across years only by its account number, and from FY2023 to FY2026 dozens of accounts appear new each year while others stop -- for example, an E.S. guidance counselor salary account (ending 511001) has no FY2026 postings, and a social workers salary account under the same org (ending 511024) first appears in FY2025; whether one continues the other is not recorded. Nothing in the journal says which old account a new one replaces, so a line moved to a new number reads as new (never compared with its own past) and the old one as a line that spent nothing, which can make a budget look set high when the cost simply moved. The budget against actual page marks every such case and does not guess. — closes: the Town Accountant's or the school business office's crosswalk of old to new account numbers (the MUNIS chart-of-accounts changes) for FY2023-FY2026.
money_outWhich games Lunenburg’s athletic teams played in the seasons their posted schedules do not cover/analysis/transportation builds its athletic bus model from the schedules the district posts on ArbiterLive, the scheduling site linked from its athletics page. ArbiterLive lists only what a coach posts: cheer posts no schedule at all, some teams post none in some years, and indoor and outdoor track list far fewer meets than the district's by-sport sheet has charges. A team with no listed game is not a team that took no bus, so the model is a floor for those teams and cannot be checked against the sheet for them. — closes: the athletic department's final game and meet schedule for each team, FY2022 to FY2026, with home and away and the venue, from the Athletic Director by records request.
money_outWhich items made up the $182,500 FY2003 capital plan voted at the May 2002 annual town meeting?capital-plans holds the approved item list from the Capital Planning Committee report (2010 p14; FY2014 onward). The 2002 report states only the total: the committee report (p12) says we were only able to have a Capital FY Plan of $182,500.00, and Article 4 (p77) votes the sum of $182,500 for the FY'03 Capital Plan and lists its funding transfers, not its items. Searched: capital plan, capital planning, capital request (pages 3, 7, 11, 12, 15, 20, 27, 75, 77, 85). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY2003 plan as presented to the May 2002 annual town meeting, or the Article 4 motion sheet.
money_outWhich ledger accounts and budget lines make up the special education share DESE reports for a mixed function?MEASURED (sources/data/sped-crosswalk.csv, /special-education/sped-definition): DESE counts special education as a PROGRAM inside a function, and the district's FY2023 and FY2024 End of Year Report working copies put part of supervision (2110), classroom teaching (2305), substitutes (2324, 2325), paraprofessionals (2330), guidance (2710) and psychology (2800) in the Special Education column. The report prints one figure per function and program; the Town's ledger and the district's budget book can be read account by account and line by line, and no document held says which accounts or lines make up each share. So the difference between DESE's total and each of our three definitions can be measured by function and cannot be traced to accounts. — closes: the district's worksheet mapping each MUNIS account to an End of Year Report line and program, FY2023 and FY2024.
money_outWhich of the three published per-sport athletics cost figures is correctNARROWED 5 October 2026: one of the three is now traced to its workbook. The Finance Committee's files hold Athletics Costs (1).xlsx, whose FY24 Programmatic Cost column (sheet ALL, rows 2-26) sums to 275,947.63 -- the published 'Athletic Program Costs by Sport' total -- once cell K26 is counted: Girls Ice Hockey, typed as the TEXT 1100, an estimate. The workbook's own printed total, 255,042.35, comes from =SUM(K3:K26), which leaves out both row 2 (Football, 19,805.28) and that text cell. So that figure was built from these rows, an estimate included; it does not say which of the three is correct. Three documents the district produced state three different costs for the same team in the same year, FY2024. Across all 25 teams they total $185,355.62 (the Athletic Program Funding Overview deck of 1 May 2024), $275,947.63 (“Athletic Program Costs by Sport”, published with the FY26 budget materials) and $349,145.39 (the Total Expenses column of the district’s own by-sport workbook, obtained by records request) — a spread of $163,789.77, 88.4%. Per team it is far wider: Boys' Lacrosse is stated at $612.79 and at $14,189.18, 2215.5% apart, and not one of the 25 teams carries the same figure in every column. The three may be answering different questions — a programmatic cost, an all-in cost and a season’s booked expenses would all differ legitimately — but no document we hold says which each column is, and nothing published reconciles them. So a resident choosing which sport to give up is choosing between figures that disagree by a multiple. — closes: a reconciliation from the district of its own three per-sport cost statements, sport by sport, naming what each column counts.
money_outWhich of the treasurer's payments in fiscal 1983 went to which vendor?report-vendor-payments holds payments to vendors over $4,000 from the 1986 report (MGL c.40 s.4G). The 1983 report prints no vendor list: the detailed statement of payments (p45-48) is by department and object, and no contracts-over-$4,000 table is printed (the earliest edition read so far that has one is 1986); searched for contracts, in excess of, $4,000 and vendor on every page and found only warrant text (p81) and a tax-exemption amount (p11) (sources/data/report-tables/1983/). — closes: the Town Accountant's accounts-payable detail behind the warrants for fiscal 1983.
money_outWhich payees received over $4,000 from the town in fiscal 1982?report-vendor-payments holds the contracts-over-$4,000 list from the 1986 report. The 1982 report prints no such list; the whole text was searched for 4,000, contracts, and in excess of (only the tax exemption $4,000 valuation and one budget line hit) (sources/data/report-tables/1982/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1982 accounts-payable detail by vendor.
money_outWhich post did the $13,691.53 of FY2025 fee-fund pay that the Town moved onto the H.S. Principal/Assistant Principal line pay?MEASURED: journal entry 2025/12/001339 (PER MEMO 08/20/2025) took $120,008.53 off the fee fund's high school salary account and put $106,317.00 on ATHLETIC COACHES and $13,691.53 on H.S. PRINCIPAL/ASST PRINCIPAL. By our arithmetic the $13,691.53 is FY2025's high school fee-fund pay ($114,671.53) less its whole-dollar part ($100,980.00). No roster names an assistant principal as director before FY2026, and the athletic secretary is said in a meeting to sit in the main office; neither settles which post it was. Shown on /athletics/athletic-director. — closes: the memo of 20 August 2025 behind journal entry 2025/12/001339.
money_outWhich providers’ tuition did the FY2026 year-end reclassification to the circuit breaker cover?In FY2026 one journal entry, RECLASS COLLABORATIVE TUITION, moved collaborative tuition from the general fund to the circuit breaker fund. A journal entry carries no payee, so /special-education/sped-providers attributes each provider’s invoices to the fund they were first paid from, and the FY2026 split by fund is unknowable from the ledger for whatever the entry moved. — closes: the supporting schedule for the FY2026 year-end reclassification of collaborative tuition, listing the invoices it moved.
money_outWhich school general fund line does each grant, circuit breaker and fee dollar pay toward, and would the general fund have paid it otherwise?MEASURED in the school journal: other funds' spending can be placed on general fund lines only by match rules of our own -- a journal entry naming both ends, the same payee, or the same function code -- and much of it matches no line at all: grant payroll booked to no function, lunch, extended day, capital articles. The books record who paid, never what the payment replaced, so whether a grant paid for something the general fund would otherwise have bought cannot be read off them. — closes: the DESE-approved budget for each FY2026 grant, by line and position, and the district's End of Year Financial Report, which states every fund's spending by DESE function.
money_outWhich school lines stopped being funded in FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025The restated figures for those years come from the FY27 budget projection workbooks, which print a shorter line list and almost no zeros. Not one line in them goes from funded in one year to a printed zero in the next — so the measurement this project can make for FY2015 through FY2022 has no evidence at all for the three most recent years. That is a property of which document restates which year, not a finding that nothing stopped. — closes: a district budget book for FY2026 or later printing the full line list with prior-year columns, in the same shape as fy24-approved-budget.
money_outWhich voted budget line the grant and revolving spending booked to no function code servedMEASURED: in the school MUNIS journal most spending outside the general fund in FY2026 posts to function 0000 or to a heading (1000, 2000, 2300, 2400, 4000), not to any line the general fund budget is voted on (/school-all-funds/budget-lines-all-funds, which shows it as its own row and does not spread it). The district's End of Year Financial Report to DESE does put grant spending on function codes, so the attribution is made somewhere outside the town's ledger. This narrows Which budget line each dollar of grant and revolving money paid for: the ledger cannot answer it either. — closes: the district's End of Year Financial Report working papers, grant and revolving columns by function, FY2023-FY2026.
money_outWho approved the $189,276.75 the school general fund paid FLLAC on 30 June 2026, on invoices numbered for FY2027, and under what authority?The school journal shows nine FLLAC invoices (27L2KEY11-19) paid on 30 June 2026 by check 218995 from the FY2026 general fund collaborative tuition line, which was already past its budget. G.L. c. 71 s. 71D lets a school committee approve tuition up to three months in advance; no School Committee minutes from April to August 2026 record such a vote. The warrant for 18 to 30 June, $362,767.40, is on the School Committee's 15 July 2026 agenda; on the recording the item is raised, the talk turns to transfers, and no warrants are approved; that meeting's minutes were never posted, and no later School Committee agenda or minutes lists the warrant. — closes: the signed warrant that paid check 218995, with the School Committee's approval of it, and any s. 71D vote for FY2027 tuition.
money_outWhy FY2024’s regular-route bus spending was higher than FY2025’sThe general fund regular-route transportation account spent more in FY2024 than in FY2025, and closed FY2024 past its revised budget even after a transfer in, while FY2025 spent its budget exactly. Both years were under the Dee Bus contract that preceded the current one, which this archive does not hold, so whether FY2024 carried an extra bus, extra routes, a price step that later reversed, or a cost booked in the wrong year cannot be told. A Finance Committee member asked for the bus contracts in March 2024. — closes: the Dee Bus contract in force for FY2024 and FY2025 with its rate schedule, and the FY2024 Dee Bus invoices (the contract was requested on 9 October 2026).
money_outWhy FY2026 private special-education tuition came in far under budget while collaborative tuition ran far overIn the FY2026 period-13 ledger the general fund’s private-tuition line (9300) ended well under budget and its collaborative-tuition line (9400) well over, netting to a small surplus; the circuit breaker fund (2640) paid collaborative tuition that year and no private tuition, the reverse of FY2025. Fewer private placements, placements moved to collaboratives, and the line a payment was charged to all fit the same rows. — closes: the FY2026 out-of-district placement list by setting, with start dates and each tuition invoice and the fund it was paid from.
money_outWhy a budget line came in under plan, as against by how muchA line under plan can be a post left vacant, a service cut, a grant that covered the cost instead, money transferred to another line, or a line over-budgeted from the start. All five produce the same smaller number in the spent column. The accounting system narrows it — it records mid-year transfers, so money moved can be distinguished from money not spent, and we hold that for FY2026 — but it cannot separate a vacancy from a cancelled service from a funding switch. Every published explanation of a Lunenburg school surplus is therefore a hypothesis about a measurement, and this project must not restate one as the measurement. — closes: payroll detail by position and date for the year in question, which separates a vacancy from every other cause, plus the grant award records for the same year.
money_outWhy a school purchase order was still open on 30 June, and why an order carried into the next year was closed with nothing paidMEASURED (/school-all-funds/carried-over-orders): at each close the school journal zeroes every open order (YEC) and reopens it on 1 July (SOY), and a carry-forward transfer raises the next year's budget by the same amount; of the general fund orders carried out of FY2023-FY2025, 68% were paid the next year and the rest closed with nothing paid against them. Neither the journal nor the period-13 reports say why an order was open at the year end (goods not delivered, an invoice not received, a deliberate hold of budget), or why a carried order was closed rather than paid, or whether what it was for was bought again on a new order (one revolving-fund order, Nature's Classroom, was closed and the same amount paid on a new one). So the size of the carry is measured and its cause is not. — closes: the district’s year-end list of open purchase orders, with the reason each was kept open or closed, FY2023-FY2026.
money_outWhy a special education line ran over its vote in a given year: a new child, a higher tuition rate, or a longer route?MEASURED (/special-education-reserve/surprise-costs): over FY2010-FY2026 out-of-district tuition was the largest share of every dollar the three special education lines ran over their votes, transportation next, in-district services last. The ledger records the overrun and not its cause; the district's own deck to the Finance Committee (22 October 2026, slide 9) names all three -- new student needs, tuition increases, transportation changes -- and every one lands as the same figure on the line. A reserve sized on the total cannot say which risk it is carrying. — closes: the district's year-end explanation of each special education line's variance, by cause.
money_outWhy has school electricity run past its voted budget in every year from FY2023 to FY2026?Account 0100-3-300-4130-99-1-74-2-521011 spent and committed $303,101.82 more than it was voted across FY2023-FY2026, and the FY2027 budget, $316,250, is below the $319,108.72 FY2026 had already paid. Natural-gas heating beside it was voted above its spending in FY2024-FY2026 and received transfers in every year. Usage, rates, load moving from gas to electricity, and the solar panels a Finance Committee member asked about on 26 February 2026 all fit. /analysis/fy26-school-surplus — closes: the school utility bills by building and month, with kilowatt-hours and any solar or net-metering credit.
money_outWhy the school department's FY2024 actual spending differs between its period 13 ledger and the general fund history, on 12 of 265 linesMeasured 5 October 2026 from the Finance Committee files: the period 13 report (glytdbud, generated 7 August 2024) and the FY2010-FY2025 general fund history agree to the cent on 253 of 265 school general-fund lines; 12 differ, by a net 243,636.29, the history higher -- led by a paraprofessional line and a clerical salary line, with some lines moving the other way. Entries posted to FY2024 after 7 August 2024 would produce this pattern; nothing here tests that. — closes: the Town Accountant's FY2024 journal entries posted after 7 August 2024 for fund 0100, department 300.
money_outWhy was the school circuit breaker fund drawn monthly in FY2025 but left almost untouched in FY2026 until 29 June?The FY2025 and FY2026 budget books both plan the circuit breaker to pay part of collaborative tuition. In FY2025 the fund paid $445,631 from July to May; in FY2026 it paid $4,005, then $333,494.89 in one re-charge on 29 June 2026, the day before $289,331 of older money would pass DESE's one-year limit. A year-end settlement chosen on purpose, a change of staff, and waiting for the state's rate all fit the same entries. -- closes: the district's FY2026 circuit breaker spending plan, or its written explanation of when and why the fund was drawn.
money_outWill the school accounts that closed FY2026 past their revised budgets be covered by year-end transfers, and from which lines?The FY2026 period-13 MUNIS report for department 300 (sources/data/munis-school-ytd.csv, run 6 October 2026) shows 57 accounts past their revised budgets by $1,201,433.81, after the ten year-end transfers the School Committee approved on 29 July 2026 ($148,364.31), whose minutes say more "may still be forthcoming". FY2025 closed with 4 such accounts; FY2023 with 70 and FY2024 with 52. The school appropriation is a bottom-line total, so this is not spending past the appropriation; it is whether the line budgets the next budget is built from say where the money goes. /analysis/fy26-school-surplus — closes: the FY2026 year-end line-item transfer schedule for department 300 as posted, by account, with the vote that authorised each.
peopleAre long-tenured homeowners being taxed out — what do households who bought decades ago earn against what they pay?The Census publishes tenure (B25038) and income by age of householder (B19049) but never the two together for a town this size; the assessor publishes the bill per parcel and nothing about the household. — closes: Census PUMS microdata for the PUMA containing Lunenburg, which carries tenure, year moved in and income per household, at the cost of covering several towns at once.
peopleAre the gross wages in Lunenburg's 2003 payroll report for calendar 2003 or fiscal 2003?The 2003 annual town report's payroll report (p96-p103) is headed PAYROLL REPORT and totalled GRAND TOTAL GROSS WAGES FOR 2003 ($12,956,848.27), and says nowhere which year it means; 2010 prints CALENDAR 2010 WAGES and FY2011 onward print fiscal-year earnings, so the 2003 rows cannot be compared with either until this is known. Searched the whole text for calendar, fiscal, W-2 and payroll (sources/data/report-tables/2003/). — closes: the Town Accountant's 2003 payroll register or the W-2 transmittal (Form W-3) total for calendar 2003.
peopleAre the gross wages in the 2006 payroll report calendar-year 2006 or fiscal-year 2006 earnings?report-gross-wages holds CALENDAR 2010 wages from the 2010 edition and FISCAL-year wages from FY2011 onward. The 2006 PAYROLL REPORT (PDF pages 112-121) prints no year and no basis on any page; its Textract text was searched for payroll, calendar and fiscal around those pages and returned only the page headings. So its 566 rows cannot be compared with either series. — closes: the Treasurer's payroll report for 2006 as run, or the W-2 totals for calendar 2006.
peopleBefore 2015, in which departments did senior tax work-off participants work?Before FY2015 the annual reports say only "various town departments and the Lunenburg Public School System". -- closes: the committee's annual placement lists (its minutes of 30 January 2012 record one being typed)
peopleDo the 2007 annual report's gross wages cover calendar 2007 or fiscal 2007?report-gross-wages is calendar earnings in the 2010 report and fiscal-year earnings from FY2011. The 2007 PAYROLL REPORT (PDF pages 110-121) prints EMPLOYEE, DEPARTMENT and GROSS WAGES and no year on any page, and the index (p3) calls it only Payroll Report; the text was searched for payroll, calendar and wages. Its rows cannot be put in a series with either kind until this is known. — closes: the Town Accountant's 2007 payroll register, or the W-2 totals for calendar 2007, against which a few named employees' figures could be matched.
peopleDo the teachers of Ashburnham-Westminster, Tyngsborough, Hudson, Maynard, Uxbridge, Shrewsbury, Nashoba, Wachusett, Groton-Dunstable, Ayer Shirley, North Middlesex and Monty Tech sit as high on their own salary schedules as Lunenburg’s?Harvard is measured (scripts/extract_peer_teacher_pay.py: its town report’s TEACHER section, on its own master’s top step, beside Lunenburg’s). Two more lists are read but cannot be placed on their own scale, because the salary schedule for the list’s year is not held: Ashburnham-Westminster’s FY2025 list (reprinted in Ashburnham’s 2025 report; the agreements held cover FY2017-FY2019 and FY2026-FY2028) and Tyngsborough’s 2022 Gross Wage Report (agreements held cover FY2019-FY2021 and FY2025-FY2027, and 2022 is the latest list the town posts); only their dollar quartiles are published. Hudson and Maynard print their school employees’ calendar-2025 pay, and Uxbridge its town and school employees’ calendar-2024 pay, by name with NO job title, so a teacher cannot be told from a custodian or a substitute. For Shrewsbury, Nashoba, Wachusett, Groton-Dunstable, Ayer Shirley, North Middlesex and Monty Tech no published list naming school employees was found in the member towns’ reports or on the districts’ sites (where each was looked for: notes/findings/WAGE-LISTS-COMPARISON-TOWNS.md). — closes: for Ashburnham-Westminster and Tyngsborough, the teachers’ agreements covering FY2025 and FY2022-FY2023; for the others, each district’s count of teachers by step and lane, or its payroll’s calendar-2025 gross earnings by employee with position title.
peopleHow many Lunenburg applicants Monty Tech turns awayLunenburg’s count at Monty Tech has risen in nine of the last twelve years, and a count is the outcome of two things at once: families applying, and Monty Tech admitting. The lottery exists precisely because more apply than there are places. Asked at the Finance Committee on 5 February 2026 how many Lunenburg students were turned away, the district’s business manager said she was unsure of the exact number. The Class of 2030 lottery result in this archive gives one cohort’s admissions — 24 Lunenburg students of 365 places — and its per-applicant pages are OCR of an image PDF and cannot be counted from. So a rising count cannot be read as rising demand, and the two have opposite implications for what the town should expect next. — closes: Monty Tech’s admissions summary by sending town and year — applications received, offers made, waitlisted — which the district produces for its own School Committee.
peopleHow many Lunenburg children are educated at private or parochial schoolsDESE publishes where a town’s resident children go to school by receiving district, every year since SY2014 — and every row is keyed on the eight-digit code that identifies a Massachusetts PUBLIC district. Private schools do not have one and do not report enrolment to the state, so a Lunenburg child at Cushing Academy, Notre Dame or St Bernard’s generates no record: not a zero, not an “other”, nothing, for any town in any year (checked across the whole table). WHAT THIS BREAKS: the count of children educated outside Lunenburg’s own schools — 177 in FY2026 — is a FLOOR and reads as a total. A resident asked why Cushing was missing before the page admitted the limit. AND IT MATTERS IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM THE REST: a child at a private school costs the town no tuition and no assessment, and moves Chapter 70 aid by about $150 a pupil, so those departures are close to free for the school budget. They are the only kind of leaving that does not cost money, and they are the kind nobody can count. IT IS NOT: evidence that the number is large, or small. Nothing here bounds it at all. — closes: the town census, which counts every resident child of school age regardless of where they enrol, or the district’s own October 1 resident count, which is compiled annually and not published.
peopleHow many Lunenburg homes have a child in the LUNENBURG PUBLIC SCHOOLS — as opposed to a child under 18?The Census answers the second and not the first. B11005 puts 1,477 of 4,529 households — 32.6% — with a child under 18, which is what people mean when they say "about 30% of taxpaying homes", and on that reading the claim is fair. But that count includes children at Monty Tech, at private and charter schools, and children not yet of school age, so it is a CEILING rather than the figure. The arithmetic suggests the gap is real: 1,477 households against roughly 1,745 school-age children is about 1.2 per household, low enough that a meaningful share of those homes have only pre-school children. Nothing published joins a child to a household to a school. — closes: a count of DISTINCT HOUSEHOLDS with at least one child enrolled, which the district can produce from its own student information system and DESE cannot, because DESE counts children and the Census counts households and neither knows about the other.
peopleHow many administrators does the district employ, and how has that changed over ten years?The annual-report rosters carry names without FTE, classify department liaisons as administrators, and print no central office at all in FY2025, so a series read off them shows administration falling by a quarter in a year in which nothing of the kind happened; DESE publishes administration only as dollars per pupil. — closes: the district’s position control list by FTE and funding source, for any two years ten apart.
peopleHow many children Chapter 70 is actually paid forThe aid is calculated on a Foundation enrollment of 1,599 in DESE’s FY27 Chapter 70 summary. DESE publishes three other counts for the same district — Student Headcount, In-District FTE Pupils and Total FTE Pupils — and in the latest year published they are 1,563, 1,568.9 and 1,665.9. Four numbers, one agency, none of them equal, measured on different dates and counting different things. So every per-pupil figure on this project, including aid per pupil, is a division by a count whose definition has to be stated with it, and no published document reconciles the foundation count to the children in the buildings. — closes: DESE’s FY27 foundation enrollment worksheet for Lunenburg, which states the October 1 count by grade and category the formula was run on.
peopleHow many children Lunenburg has with disabilities, given that DESE publishes three different countsNARROWED, 8 September 2026, and the narrowing is itself the finding. The denominator behind the staffing ratios in yamx-769q is NOT unexplained: it equals the published IN-DISTRICT count exactly, in all six years the file covers, and the difference between it and the count printed beside it is the published out-of-district count to the child. Computed on every build by scripts/build_special_education.py, which fails rather than publishing the page if it stops reconciling. WHAT SURVIVES is a THIRD count: dese_sped_movement reports 10 to 26 fewer children on an IEP than dese_sped_program in every overlapping year, on a different enrollment figure, and nothing published states the census date or the inclusion rule behind either. — closes: DESE’s SIMS submission detail for Lunenburg stating the census date and the inclusion rule behind each published count.
peopleHow many children enter or leave an out-of-district placement during a school year, and when?Only two snapshots are published, months apart and taken by different bodies: DESE's count of students with disabilities placed out of district in October, and the town's count of placements on 1 March in the Special Services report of each annual town report. Their difference is a NET change -- an arrival and a departure between the two dates cancel, and a child placed and returned between them is in neither -- and some of it may be the two bodies counting differently. DESE's caseload-movement file (8aww-sugs) counts children entering and leaving special education SERVICES, not placements. The district has said at public meetings that children have moved in already needing a placement and that a child entering after 1 April is the sending district's cost; neither is a count. A mid-year reserve for tuition is sized by exactly this number, which is why /analysis/special-education-costs cannot size one from children and sizes it from the ledger instead. — closes: the district's out-of-district placement log, one row per placement with its start date, end date and setting (collaborative, day or residential) and no names, from the Director of Student Services by records request.
peopleHow many children play sportsTwo town documents give 593 and 649 for the same year and count different things: one counts fee categories, the other counts participations by sport, and a participation is not a child — one student playing three seasons is three of them. Some workbook rows are negative, subtracting out-of-district athletes back out, so a season total is a net figure rather than a headcount of bodies. Nothing published is an unduplicated count. — closes: an unduplicated athlete roster, or a participation report that states whether it counts students or participations.
peopleHow many children ride the school buses, and how many pay the feeThe only count in the record is the Superintendent's report to the School Committee on 4 June 2025 of bus requests received, and how many were unpaid, for the first fee year. A request is not a rider and an unpaid request is not a refusal. Without riders, no cost per rider and no share of the bus cost covered by the fee can be computed, and whether the fee changed ridership cannot be seen. — closes: the district's transportation registration count for each school year by grade band, fee tier (one child, family, reduced, free) and paid status, with the ridership counts the routes are planned on.
peopleHow many hours did senior tax work-off participants put in at each department, in any season?Every annual report prints one total of hours across all departments, and none before FY2015 names the departments (/homes-and-taxes/senior-tax-work-off). -- closes: the timesheets the Assistant Town Manager/HR Director returns to the Assessors each November (policy VI.D.3-4), tallied by department
peopleHow many hours did senior tax work-off participants work in the 2023 season, and in which departments?The FY2023 annual report has no program section; the Assessors' minutes of 26 February 2024 give only "under $9,363.65 for 11 individuals". -- closes: the HR Director's 2023 program summary, the text the other annual reports print
peopleHow many of Lunenburg’s teachers sit on each step and lane of the salary schedule, each year?DESE’s Teachers function grew while teacher FTE fell, so spending per teacher FTE rose. An average moves with raises, with teachers moving up steps and lanes, and with who is on staff (fewer, more senior teachers raise it with nobody’s pay changing), and DESE publishes no count by step or lane, so the three cannot be told apart. See /school-spending-history/pay-or-headcount. — closes: the district’s count of teachers on each step and lane of the salary schedule, for each year.
peopleHow many of the children who leave Lunenburg under school choice have an IEPDESE publishes where every town’s resident children are enrolled, by district and by programme — 58 leaving under school choice in SY2026, 22 at charter schools, 97 at Montachusett Regional as members — and publishes NO disability status with it. So a special education student who transfers out and a student with no plan who transfers out are one row. This is why /where-students-go-instead is a separate report from the other three special education pages rather than a section inside one: merged, “58 children left” becomes “58 special education children left” in a single retelling. — closes: DESE’s SIMS detail crossing enrollment reason with IEP status, which is not published at town level at all.
peopleHow many out-of-district placements are children who arrived already placedThe trajectory file measures the route through the district’s own settings, and the district told the School Committee on 4 February 2026 that “we have also had students move into the district that require out of district placements”. Such a child enters the town’s placement count without ever appearing in a cohort followed from an in-district setting, so the count and the route measure overlapping but different populations. The quote is evidence that it happens; nothing establishes how often, and the two published counts of placed children — the town’s on 1 March and DESE’s — agree in only 2 of the 5 years they overlap. — closes: the district’s own record of placements by origin, showing how many were referred from an in-district setting and how many arrived already placed.
peopleHow many paraprofessionals Lunenburg needs, against how many it employs603 CMR 28.06(6)(d) is now in this archive, and it sets the class-size rule everybody argues around: a substantially separate group may not exceed eight students to one certified special educator, or twelve to a special educator AND AN AIDE. So a paraprofessional is partly what PERMITS a larger group rather than being a ratio in itself — which means paraprofessional counts track PROGRAM STRUCTURE and not student headcount, and would explain the thing /school-staffing measures and cannot account for: paras rising while enrolment fell. WHAT STILL CANNOT BE COMPUTED: the regulation binds INSTRUCTIONAL GROUPS and nothing published says how many groups Lunenburg runs, how large each is, or how its 41 substantially separate students are divided among them. 41 students could be four groups or seven, needing very different staffing, and both are lawful. THREE THINGS THAT WOULD DEFEAT ANY RATIO ANYWAY, all in the regulation itself: the sizes are MAXIMUMS and districts are expected to go smaller for complex needs (28.06(6)(c)); grouping must match each student’s own IEP, which can require one-to-one support no class-size rule predicts (b); and a group at maximum may take two further students mid-year by decision of the Administrator of Special Education (e). IT IS NOT: evidence that staffing is too high or too low. Nothing here supports either. — closes: the district’s own list of special education instructional groups by school and setting, with the students and staff assigned to each — compiled for DESE’s program approval under 603 CMR 28.09 and not published.
peopleHow many people each TOWN department employs, in FTE, in a form that can be counted the same way twiceCORRECTED. This row previously said the only published series stops at FY2016, when the gross-wages list stopped tagging each name with a department. That is true of the WAGE LIST and it is not true of the reports. Every annual report carries departments describing their own staffing in the prose of their narrative section -- 77 such statements across FY2011 to FY2025, in every year. The Fire Department gives a series on its own: 5 Career and 40-45 On Call in FY2017, 7 Career from FY2018, 10 Career and 30-35 On Call/Per Diem from FY2022. The DPW states its establishment post by post: one Director, one Executive Assistant shared with Facilities, one Highway Superintendent, 5 Heavy Equipment Operators, one Mechanic, one Cemetery Superintendent, two Seasonal Cemetery Laborers, one Sewer Business Manager and one Assistant. The Building Department, the Council on Aging and the Assessor's office do the same. WHAT REMAINS A GAP is that none of it is FTE and none of it is consistent: a range (30-45 on call), a headcount, and a list of titles are three different quantities, stated in whichever form that year's department head chose, and they cannot be summed into a town total or compared like for like across departments. -- closes: the town's payroll register by department, or the personnel schedule behind the omnibus budget, which sets an FTE per line before Town Meeting votes it.
peopleHow many people the schools actually employThe town publishes per-school staff ROSTERS in every annual report, FY2011 to FY2025 — a list of names. A roster carries no FTE, so a 0.4 music teacher and a full-timer are one row each, and it is a point in time, undated within the year. A count of names the town printed is a real quantity and it is not a staffing level. AND THE DISTRICT’S OWN CONTACT SHEETS DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER, which this project did not know until it held them: its roll-up of every employee names 257 people, the five listings the office and the four schools keep name 45 the roll-up does not, and the roll-up names people no building lists — Primary leaves its own paraprofessionals off the sheet the school keeps. Some of that difference is one person written two ways (Skye Abreu on one, Skye Abrue on the other) and nothing published distinguishes a second spelling from a second person, because no sheet carries an employee identifier. So there is no count of district staff here that two documents support. — closes: a staffing report stating FTE by position and year.
peopleHow many people work in the offices voted as General Government — the Town Manager, the Town Clerk, the Treasurer/Collector and Information TechnologyNine town departments now state a headcount somewhere in their own report, but General Government is voted as ONE figure covering several offices and only the Assessing office inside it states a number. Health & Sanitation, Central Purchasing, Solid Waste and Employee benefits state none at all. The gross-wages list named a department beside each employee through FY2016 and stopped — closes: the Town’s gross wages list with its department column restored, or any payroll headcount by department.
peopleHow many residents took part in the 2013 senior tax work-off season, and for how many hours?The FY2013 annual report has no program section, and the Assessors folded the credits into all exemptions (Board of Assessors minutes, 10 December 2013). -- closes: the Assessors' FY2014 list of work-off credits under c.59 s.5K
peopleHow many school choice seats Lunenburg opened, by grade and by yearChildren arriving from other towns fell from 51 in SY2014 to 15 in SY2026. Two readings fit that equally well and the published record separates them in one year only. A receiving district DECIDES each year how many school choice seats to open and at which grades — the School Committee minutes record that decision being taken on 22 January 2025 (elementary seats against high school only, tabled until the budget was settled), on 16 April 2025 (options beyond grade 9, moved contingent on free cash passing) and on 4 February 2026 (“We are looking to only add school choice options to the high school”). So fewer arrivals is consistent with fewer seats offered and equally consistent with fewer families applying. The Superintendent stated both counts to the Finance Committee on 26 February 2026 — 24 seats opened, 5 students applied — which points at applications for that one year and cannot speak for the other twelve. — closes: the School Committee’s annual school choice vote, seats by grade, for every year from SY2014 onward; the minutes hold it in pieces and nobody has compiled it as a series.
peopleHow many school employees are enrolled in the district’s active health insurance, and on which plan tiers?NARROWED 5 October 2026. the Finance Committee files received by records request on 4 October 2026 (sources/budget-workbooks/finance-committee/, see its PROVENANCE note) include a school department presentation whose second page counts active subscribers by plan for FY26 budgeting: HMO Blue family 110, HMO Blue individual 32, Blue Care Elect family 19, individual 9, Blue Select 1 -- 171 in all. A district slide, not the carrier's census; the per-employee sheet behind it is held privately and not cited. The $3,701,195 FY2026 active line is the largest piece of the schools’ $5.22M health insurance and no document states its headcount. The Town Manager’s FY27 Unclassified presentation (12 March 2026, pp. 6–7) gives the town side to the person — 55 town actives, 67 town retirees, 203 school retirees, November 2025 enrollment — and the school active side only as a method (FY25 Superintendent’s budget update, p. 41: “counting all staff currently subscribing”). Subscribers are not people covered: a family plan is one subscriber. — closes: the MIIA renewal census by plan tier for the school department, or the PEC negotiation packet; both exist and neither is published.
peopleHow many students played a school sport in each of the last ten years?The district has published season participation counts for three years (FY2024–FY2026), and the archive holds no earlier ones; a ten-year trend in athletes cannot be drawn. — closes: the athletic department’s season participation reports for FY2016–FY2023, which the department compiles each season.
peopleHow many teachers Lunenburg employed before FY2008Net school spending and the 1 October enrolment count are published from FY1994; DESE’s teacher file starts with FY2008 and the town’s printed school rosters with FY2011, and a roster carries no FTE. So the first part of the long-run comparison on /school-spending-history has spending and pupils and no teachers beside them, and the teacher line can only be drawn from FY2008 — closes: any DESE staffing report for Lunenburg before FY2008, or the district’s own staffing history by year.
peopleHow much of a department’s headcount is full-timeA roster counts the Council on Aging's Tuesday van driver and its Director as one each. ONE FTE FIGURE DOES EXIST and this row used to deny it: the FY2025 Finance Committee report states the FY2026 school budget “necessitates eliminating approximately 28 Full-Time Equivalents (39 employees)”, which also measures the gap between posts and people — 39 people in 28 FTE. That is one department in one year; no FTE is published for any other department or any other year — closes: an FTE schedule, or the wage list read in full.
peopleHow much of each teacher’s gross pay is base salary, and how much is stipends, coaching, longevity or summer work?The town’s annual reports print every town and school employee’s gross pay for the calendar year, by name, and joined to the school rosters it gives a distribution of teacher pay (see /school-spending-history/teachers-on-the-scale). But gross pay is ONE figure per person: it folds the schedule cell together with stipends, coaching, longevity, summer work and any retroactive pay, and a calendar year straddles two contract years. So a teacher paid more than a lane’s top step may be on that step, or lower in a higher lane, or lower with extra duties, and the list cannot tell which. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: where any teacher sits on the schedule. — closes: the district’s payroll earnings report for the year, by employee and earnings code (base, stipend, longevity, coaching), counts only, or the step-and-lane placement count itself.
peopleHow much of the property tax levy is paid by households headed by someone 65 or over?The Census now gives income by age of householder — a household headed by someone 65 or over has a median income of $72,935 ± $8,677, against $129,183 ± $21,150 for a 45-to-64 household — and that is income, not tax. The override argument is about a BILL: what a $3,000,000 override adds to a household is quoted at meetings as a town-wide average, and the town publishes no split of the levy by who pays it, by age or by anything else. Nor does it publish how many households take the statutory elderly exemptions and abatements that would change the answer. So "seniors on fixed incomes cannot carry it" cannot be checked in either direction, and neither can its opposite. — closes: the Board of Assessors’ commitment list with the Clause 41A, 41C and 17D exemptions granted, joined to the town census by age of owner — both held by the Town and neither published.
peopleIs a rate printed in a town salary schedule the rate that was paid, and is the schedule itself internally consistent?The Salary Administration Plan schedule voted at the 2022 annual town meeting -- page 152 of the FY2022 annual report -- prints 20 grades against 8 steps and NO TOTAL of any kind, so nothing on the page tests its own figures. Its 160 hourly rates sit about 3% apart step to step and no single rounding rule reproduces them: round(step 1 x 1.03^(n-1)) misses 50 of the 140 derived cells, and grade 2 step 2 computes 15.38 where the page prints 15.37. The reading is safe because the page carries its own text layer and the characters are exact, but the DOCUMENT has no internal check a reader could apply, and a typo in a published schedule would be invisible. Separately, the schedule says what a grade and step pay per hour and says nothing about who is in which grade, at which step, or for how many hours -- so it cannot be turned into what the town spent on anyone. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the printed rates are the rates the payroll system actually applied. -- closes: the Personnel Committee’s own rate table as submitted to the Town Clerk, which the warrant says is on file, read against the payroll register for the same year.
peopleIs the 2008 annual report's payroll (gross wages by employee) for calendar 2008 or for fiscal 2008?The Payroll Report (PDF pages 100-110; index Payroll Report 98-108) heads its columns EMPLOYEE | DEPARTMENT | GROSS WAGES and prints no year at all. The 2010 report prints CALENDAR 2010 WAGES; FY2011 onward print fiscal-year earnings. The text of pages 100-110 was searched for any year, FISCAL, CALENDAR, YEAR and TOTAL and returned nothing, so the 585 rows land in report-gross-wages with their period not established and must not be summed or compared with either basis. — closes: the Treasurer's or Town Accountant's statement of the period the 2008 payroll report covers (or the W-2 totals for calendar 2008).
peopleWere the wages printed in Lunenburg's 2009 annual town report earned in calendar 2009 or in fiscal 2009?The payroll pages (PDF pages 84-89) print NAME, DEPT. and WAGES with no heading naming a year or a basis; the index (p5) calls them only Payroll Report. The 2010 edition prints CALENDAR 2010 WAGES and FY2011 onward print fiscal-year earnings, so this year cannot be placed beside either. Textract text searched for calendar, fiscal, W-2, gross and wages: calendar appears only in department narratives (p18, p22, p33, p45), never on or near the payroll pages (sources/data/report-tables/2009/). — closes: the Town's 2009 payroll report as run by the Treasurer or Accountant, with its date range.
peopleWhat Lunenburg’s counsellors, social workers and psychologists do, as a seriesNone of them is a teacher on DESE’s teacher returns, so the FTE files that carry fifteen years of teaching staff carry none of these people. The state’s educator retention file reaches them for three years only (FY2021–FY2023), as headcount rather than FTE, and folds them into two residual buckets named Other - Licensed and Other - Non-Licensed. The town’s annual report rosters name them every year FY2011–FY2025 and carry no FTE, no funding source and no date within the year. The district itself holds the missing instrument: it told the School Committee on 6 December 2023, while deciding what to cut, that “Information is broken out to social worker caseloads by bui lding”. That document is not published. Public comment at the same board on 24 January 2024 named MassHealth reimbursement and outside agencies as ways to pay for the same work, which is why a count without a funding source cannot answer the question anybody is asking. — closes: the per-building social worker and adjustment counsellor caseload the district prepared for the FY2025 budget, with FTE and funding source, which is a records request rather than a download.
peopleWhat a DESE special education FTE and a district special education budget line have in commonDESE's dese_sped_indicator publishes special education paraprofessionals per 100 students with disabilities; times the published count that implies about 18 FTE for SY2026 against a district paraprofessional line that has roughly doubled since SY2019, which works out at some $69,000 per FTE. A paraprofessional does not cost $69,000, so the two are not measurements of the same population. The EPIMS Data Handbook gives half the reason: it defines FTE as “the percent of workday staff are involved in an assignment” — per ASSIGNMENT, not per person — while a budget line pays whole salaries. The other half is vocabulary: the district calls a line Special Ed Paraprofessionals and DESE has its own definition of a paraprofessional on the return, and neither is wrong. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is that the two figures cannot both describe the same set of people. WHAT IS NOT is which is narrower, or by how much, or whether the line carries anything besides paraprofessionals. — closes: the district’s own crosswalk between its budget line names and what it reports to the state on EPIMS, which may exist nowhere in writing and would then be a records request rather than a download.
peopleWhat each town department spends on wages, so departments can be compared by payroll rather than by headcountThe town prints a Town & School Employee Gross Wages list every year, name by name — but it stopped printing the DEPARTMENT beside each name after FY2016, so the list cannot be split by department. Joining the names to the rosters we hold matches only a third to a half of them, so any departmental total built this way would rank our reading of the scan rather than the town’s payroll. THE REASON RECORDED HERE UNTIL 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 WAS WRONG: it said the two-column layout loses the second column’s given names, which was a measurement of OUR OCR CACHE written down as a fact about the town’s typesetting. The FY2019 pages print both columns in full, and a re-read lifted that year from 44 names to 516 in gross-wages.csv, and a reading of the pages themselves on 2 October 2026 found the pages print 599 -- so 83 names are in no dataset, 65 of them on PDF page 200 alone. 516 was a count of OUR dataset; 599 is a count of the town’s page. Nothing from it is published for that reason — closes: the wage list with its department column restored, or any payroll report by department.
peopleWhat grade-and-step hourly rates did the town's non-union salary schedule carry for 2002 or fiscal 2003?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan hold the Schedule A salary schedule and classification plan (2010 p85-86; FY2011 onward). The 2002 report prints neither: its Textract text was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, schedule a and step, and the hits are an inspection schedule (p21), the debt repayment schedule heading (p64-65), a school STEP program (p39) and the word step in prose and names. — closes: the Personnel Bylaw's Schedule A as in force for fiscal 2003, from the Town Clerk or the May 2002 annual town meeting warrant.
peopleWhat hourly rate did each grade and step of Lunenburg's non-union salary schedule pay in FY2004?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan hold the town's Schedule A grade-and-step rates and class titles (2010 p85-p86). The 2003 annual town report prints neither: its Textract text was searched for salary schedule, classification, Schedule A, point value, step, merit and personnel by-law, and returned only the accountant's SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS headings (p54-p59) and Art 7/02 ATM merit appropriation notes (p58-p59) (sources/data/report-tables/2003/). — closes: the Schedule A salary schedule and classification plan of the town's personnel by-law in force for FY2004.
peopleWhat raises did Lunenburg’s teachers’ agreements give before FY2025?The only teachers’ agreement held is the one running 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2027 (sources/contracts/), so the schedule adjustments behind the rise in spending per teacher from FY2009 to FY2024 are not known. — closes: the Lunenburg Education Association agreements before the current one, from the district or as filed with DESE.
peopleWhat share of a post any non-teaching adult in a school holdsDESE publishes a full-time equivalent for TEACHERS at school level and for nobody else. There is no published FTE — in any file, in any year — for a paraprofessional, an administrator, a nurse, a counsellor, a custodian or a kitchen post at a named school in this town. The one job-class table DESE publishes (dese_educator_workforce) is DISTRICT-only and carries headcount rather than FTE. So a school panel can say Lunenburg High printed 64 names and that 35.8 full-time-equivalent TEACHING posts sat among them, and it cannot say what the other 28 names amount to. The difference between a roster count and a teaching FTE is not part-timers — it is everybody the FTE file does not cover. — closes: DESE’s EPIMS work-assignment detail by job classification and school, or the district’s own staffing plan stating FTE by building and post.
peopleWhat the children who leave the district cost, as against how many there areThe COUNTS are published and this project now holds them: DESE’s enrollment of town residents by district (dataset vxt3-k35x) states, for every school year from SY2014 to SY2026, how many Lunenburg residents attend each other district and under which programme. SY2026: 58 children under School Choice, 22 at charter schools and 97 at Montachusett Regional as members rather than by choice. The companion file (8xyg-59b2) counts the children arriving the other way, 11 in SY2026. So "a fall in enrollment is not a count of departures" is no longer a reason to refuse the question — the departures are counted. What is NOT published anywhere in this archive is the MONEY: not one document states the tuition Lunenburg is assessed for those 58 children, or for the 22 at charters, and the two rates are set differently and are higher for special education. — closes: DLS Cherry Sheet CS 1-EB (estimated charges) for Lunenburg, which prints the school choice sending and charter tuition assessments on their own lines.
peopleWhat the corrected paraprofessional salary scale costs, and what was underpaidThe School Committee approved a corrected paraprofessional scale on 7 October 2026: 107 of 120 hourly rates rose, steps 1-8 by about 4% (FY2026-FY2027) and 4.5% (FY2028), and the top steps did not move. Draft agreements released with it offer a lump sum of FY2027 retroactive pay and one personal day in exchange for a Wage Act waiver covering FY2026 and part of FY2027; the Superintendent's estimate is about 52 people. The cost cannot be computed: the scale is a full-year figure at 6.5 hours a day, and nothing published says how many paraprofessionals sit in each column and step or on what hours, nor what each was actually paid. See notes/findings/PARA-SALARY-CORRECTION.md. — closes: payroll's calculation of the FY2027 retroactive payment (headcount by column, step and appointed hours, with the sums), or the costing put to the School Committee for the 7 October vote.
peopleWhat the special education staffing ratio requires moment to moment603 CMR 28.06(6) sets the group sizes everybody quotes — eight students to one certified special educator, twelve with an aide — and residents are asking a further question the regulation does not answer: what happens when the group splits, when students go to recess or specials, or when the teacher leaves the room. THE FULL TEXT WAS SEARCHED. There is no mention of recess, none of "under the direction of", nothing about a group dividing, and nothing about a teacher stepping out. The only supervision clause is general and applies to every student in the Commonwealth: "The school staff shall at all times provide appropriate supervision of students while they are engaged in any school related activity on or off school grounds."
