And 28.06(6) says nothing about an aide beyond the two group-size clauses — it never defines what an aide does, what qualifications one needs, or whether one may supervise alone. WHAT THIS MEANS: the ratio governs THE SIZE OF AN INSTRUCTIONAL GROUP, not the staffing of a moment. It is not a supervision rule and cannot be read as one, in either direction — it neither permits nor forbids a paraprofessional holding a group while the teacher steps out. This is the second time this regulation has turned out to bind less than people assume. — closes: the district’s own program descriptions filed for DESE approval under 603 CMR 28.09, which describe staffing as operated rather than as capped; an individual IEP, which CAN specify one-to-one support at named times and is the only document that binds a moment; and the paraprofessional provisions of the collective bargaining agreement, for duties and coverage.
peopleWhat was the Town's non-union salary schedule (grade by step) and classification plan in 2006?salary-schedule and the 2010 edition's classification plan read Schedule A from the Salary Administration Plan article. The 2006 annual town report prints no Schedule A: its Textract text was searched for salary schedule, schedule a, point value, classification and salary administration, and returned only the appropriation-schedule heading SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS (pp50-55) and three warrant articles funding a merit increase under the Salary Administration Plan (pp90, 108, 111) without its rates. — closes: the Salary Administration Plan, Schedule A, in force for FY2007, from the Town Clerk or the Human Resources office.
peopleWhat were Lunenburg's non-union grade-and-step pay rates and job classifications in 2009?The 2010 edition prints Schedule A, the salary schedule and classification plan adopted under Article 5 (salary-schedule, report-classification-plan). The 2009 edition prints neither: its Textract text was searched for schedule a, step, point value, class title, classification and salary schedule, and returned only the appropriation schedule's own heading (pp49-53), Personnel Committee prose saying it was developing a major revamp of the Salary Schedule (p22), and town meeting articles amending the Salary Administration Plan's holiday and merit provisions (p74, p77) without printing the schedule; step hits only a school programme name (p39) and a merit article (p77). — closes: the Salary Administration Plan bylaw's Schedule A as in force for 2009, from the Town Clerk.
peopleWhat were the town's non-union grade-and-step hourly rates and job classifications in 2004?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan hold Schedule A (grade by step) and the classification plan from the 2010 report (p85-86). The 2004 report prints neither: Textract text searched for salary schedule, point value, classification (hits only the accountant's SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS p55-60 and p99) and schedule a (p27, 76, 77, 100, all unrelated). The only reference is ATM 2004 Article 3 (p95), which names the Salary Administration Plan of the Town of Lunenburg voted May 2003 and was PASSED OVER. — closes: the Salary Administration Plan as voted at the May 2003 Annual Town Meeting, with its Schedule A.
peopleWhat were the town's non-union grade-and-step hourly rates, and the classification plan behind them, for fiscal 2009?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan read Schedule A (Salary Schedule and Classification Plan), which the 2010 report prints at PDF pages 85-86. The 2008 annual town report prints neither: its Textract text was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, point value, step and grade; the only hit is Article 5 (p92), which adjusts the Grade Step and Merit ranges up 2% in prose without printing the schedule, and the Personnel Committee report (p24-25), which mentions the article. — closes: the Salary Administration Plan Schedule A as amended by Article 5 of the May 2008 Annual Town Meeting.
peopleWhat were the town's non-union grade-and-step pay rates and job classifications adopted for fiscal 2006?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan read Schedule A from the 2010 report (pp 85-86). The 2005 report does not print it: the text was searched for salary schedule, classification and step, and returned only Article 8 (PDF pages 86 and 93), which amends the plan by reference to the Classification & Salary Schedule proposed by the Personnel Board and appearing in the Report of the Finance Committee with a copy on file in the Selectmen's and Town Clerk's office. — closes: the Finance Committee's report to the 2005 Annual Town Meeting, or the Salary Administration Plan Schedule A effective July 1, 2005.
peopleWhat were the town's non-union grade-and-step pay rates and job classifications for fiscal 2008?salary-schedule and report-classification-plan read the Schedule A salary schedule and classification plan the 2010 report prints with its town meeting articles. The 2007 report's town meeting excerpts (PDF pages 87-109) mention the Salary Administration Plan only by name (p89, a 3% merit increase of $13,700.00) and print no schedule: the text was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, point value and grade, and returned nothing of the kind. — closes: the Town's Salary Administration Plan, Schedule A, as in force for FY2008.
peopleWhen an agenda was actually POSTED, and so whether a meeting had its 48 hours’ noticeThe Open Meeting Law requires 48 hours’ notice excluding weekends and holidays, and NOTHING THE TOWN PUBLISHES SAYS WHEN AN AGENDA WENT UP. Checked rather than assumed: the AgendaCenter listing that every agenda is fetched from was searched in full for posted, published, uploaded, created and modified, and for any date-bearing attribute — zero occurrences of any of them. The row carries the MEETING date and nothing else. Two things stand in for it and neither is the answer. A PDF’s own creation timestamp is a LOWER BOUND on posting, since a file cannot be posted before it is made — the School Committee Policy Sub-Committee agenda of 25 September 2026 was created at 14:29 the previous afternoon, so the most notice possible for that file was 19 hours, and whether that is the notice actually given is not established. The AgendaCenter also allows a file to be replaced in place, so an earlier version could have been posted earlier and overwritten. And our own first_seen is worse, because it measures US. The watcher did not run on 18, 22 or 24 September 2026, so a document first seen on the 25th could have been posted on any of three days. A gap in the crawl silently becomes a gap in what can be said. — closes: the AgendaCenter’s posting log, which CivicEngage records internally and the site does not display; the Town Clerk can produce it.
peopleWhere 16 of Lunenburg’s students with disabilities are placed, in FY2026DESE’s placement breakdown prints four categories — Full Inclusion, Partial Inclusion, Substantially Separate and Separate School in District — and in FY2026 they sum to 242 of the 258 the same file prints as the total. Element DOE034 has nine acceptable values and this breakdown is in-district only, so the other 16 children are in categories the file does not print, and nothing published says which. That bounds every reading of the placement mix: the four printed rows are not a partition, and adding them and treating the result as the whole is the same error as summing a column that was never the total’s parts. — closes: DESE’s full DOE034 distribution for Lunenburg, or the district’s 1 October SIMS placement submission.
peopleWhether Lunenburg’s paraprofessionals moved out of special education, or were recoded, or the state changed what it countsTwo DESE files count Lunenburg paraprofessionals over FY2020–FY2025 and move in opposite directions. The district comparison sheet’s all-programmes Paraprofessional FTE rises 57.0 to 67.0; the special education staff table in n62c-bx65 falls 44.0 to 20.0, at every one of the five year-steps, while the number of children with a plan goes 244 to 238. The difference between the two therefore goes from 13.0 to 47.0 FTE. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is that the two published series diverge. WHAT IS NOT is why: paraprofessionals moving onto general education assignments, the same people being recoded, and a change in what the state’s special education staff table counts all produce this shape, and subtracting one file from the other assumes the second sits inside the first, which nothing published says. This matters because the town’s own in-district special education escalator is built on a paraprofessional budget line. — closes: Lunenburg’s EPIMS work assignment detail by job classification and program area, year by year, which would show whether the same people were reported under a different code.
peopleWhether a budgeted position was filledA budget line is money the town has to raise, not a person in a chair. A line funded all year for a post vacant half of it looks identical on the page to one that was filled. Bounded, not settled: the rosters show who was printed, which narrows the question without answering it. — closes: a filled-position list, or payroll by position rather than by name.
peopleWhether a department cut SERVICE, as opposed to cutting dollars or peopleA budget line that falls is not a cut and a headcount that falls is not a service reduction -- the thing a resident notices is hours, response times, programmes and waits. The annual reports do carry that: every year's department narratives print activity statistics such as calls for service, items circulated, patron visits, permits issued and inspections performed. None of it is extracted, and it is prose rather than tables, which is the same reason fifteen years of out-of-district placement counts went unread. Until it is read, no claim that a department held its service level while another cut can be tested in either direction. -- closes: nothing external is needed. This one is ours to do -- the figures are already in documents the archive holds.
peopleWhether a fall in a department’s headcount is a post being cut or a post standing emptyA roster is people IN post; a cut removes a POST. The two come apart both ways — somebody leaves a funded post and the count falls with nothing cut, or a post is eliminated and its holder moves into another vacancy so the count holds. The Assessing office reported being “fully staffed for the first time in over a year” in FY2024, which is a year of posts that existed and stood empty and would have read here as a smaller department. Only the DPW and the Assessing office publish an establishment at all — closes: an authorised-post schedule, or a vacancy report, for any department.
peopleWhether a position the district announced it would cut was removedThe district publishes a cut list most budget cycles — 158 named reductions across five cycles in this archive — and nothing published says what became of any of them. The only independent series that reaches any of it is DESE teacher FTE by school and subject, one October snapshot a year, and teachers are a minority of every list: paraprofessionals, secretaries, custodians, guidance staff, social workers, maintenance and BCBAs are counted by nothing at school level. A list of intended cuts is not a record of staffing. — closes: the district’s year-end position control report — filled posts by FTE, school and funding source — which the Business Office produces for payroll and does not publish.
peopleWhether a rise in the paraprofessional line is more posts or a grant unwindingDESE now publishes the split at the level of its own FUNCTION CODES, SY2009-SY2025: Lunenburg's function 2330, Paraprofessionals, is $1,338,477 of general fund beside $478,097 of grants and revolving money in SY2025 (dese_function_expenditure). That BOUNDS the question and does not settle it. A function code aggregates many posts and many funding sources; it is DESE's measure of spending rather than the town's appropriation; and nothing in it says which post any dollar paid, or whether the same posts were general-funded the year before. The in-district special education escalator still rests on a line that cannot be distinguished from grant money unwinding. — closes: the district's grant award and payroll charge detail for the paraprofessional posts, by fund and fiscal year.
peopleWhether an aide assigned to one child also counts as the aide that raises a group from eight students to twelve603 CMR 28.06(6)(c) and (d) raise the maximum group size from eight students to twelve when the certified special educator is "assisted by one aide". The regulation never defines the aide, never states their duties, and — searched on every build for eight phrasings — contains NO rule about one-to-one support of any kind. So where a child’s IEP assigns an aide to that child, nothing published says whether that person also satisfies the tier. THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS THE POINT: assuming they do understates the staffing a group needs, and assuming they do not overstates it, so neither assumption is safe and this project makes neither. It is the same wall as the paraprofessional gap, hit from the other side — the rule counts students and the staffing record counts posts, and nothing converts one into the other. — closes: DESE’s program approval materials under 603 CMR 28.09, which describe how each approved group is staffed; or the district’s own group descriptions naming which adults are counted against which tier.
peopleWhether an announced cut was reversed by a hire during the school yearResidents describe posts being cut in the spring and filled again a month into the school year. The one instrument that reaches teacher staffing is DESE’s EPIMS return, collected on 1 October, so a post cut in June and refilled in November is invisible to it and a post filled on 1 October and vacated in January counts as filled. Nothing in this archive is a within-year series. — closes: the district’s monthly payroll position report, or the School Committee’s personnel action items compiled as a series — the minutes carry appointments one meeting at a time and nobody has assembled them.
peopleWhether an “aide” in the class-size regulation is a paraprofessional the town budgets603 CMR 28.06(6) sets every group size in terms of a certified special educator AND AN AIDE — a group of eight becomes lawful at twelve because an aide is present. 28.02(3) defines the certified special educator in full and the regulation defines no counterpart for the aide anywhere; the word “paraprofessional” appears in the whole of 603 CMR 28.00 only in the staff-training clauses of 28.03(1)(a), one of which names “teachers, paraprofessionals, and teacher assistants” as three separate things. DESE’s staffing return and every Lunenburg budget line say paraprofessional. So the term that DECIDES whether a group of twelve is lawful cannot be matched to any post the town funds, and a count of paraprofessionals is not a count of aides in the regulation’s sense. This sits directly under the gap about how many paraprofessionals the town needs: even with the group list, the units would not match. — closes: DESE’s guidance on what qualifies a person as an aide for 603 CMR 28.06(6), or the district’s own job descriptions mapped to that clause.
peopleWhether the FY2026 spending on the kindergarten aide lines paid for aides in kindergarten classroomsThe ledger books FY2026 spending to two accounts titled kindergarten aides and kindergarten paraprofessionals (orgs S2032121 and S2032131), both voted at $0; a Finance Committee minute of 12 January 2026 records the School Committee chair saying kindergarten classrooms had no aides. An account title is not a person in a room: staff coded to the line while assigned elsewhere, a reclassification, or posts moved between lines all print the same ledger, and nothing published joins the account to a building. — closes: the FY2026 payroll distribution for the two accounts, naming position and building (names may be redacted).
peopleWhich budget line paid the athletic director from FY2011 to FY2017?MEASURED: the district's budget books print the Athletic Director line at $0 in FY2014 to FY2017 (actuals), and its FY19 athletics document prints no director on either the town or the fee-fund side; yet the Town's gross wages (calendar years, every fund) print the director at $98,669.28 in 2014, $96,998.30 in 2015 and $112,208.61 in 2017. The FY25 budget book says the post was made full-time in FY19 and was part-time before. So the director was paid from some other line or lines, and which is not in any document held. Shown on /athletics/athletic-director. — closes: payroll account detail for the athletic director, FY2011 to FY2017, naming the account each payment was charged to.
peopleWhich building a shared school employee actually works in, and for how much of the weekTwenty-eight people are printed as staff by more than one Lunenburg school on the schools’ own listings, one of them by four of them. THAT REPETITION IS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOTHING MORE: it is consistent with a specialist splitting a week between two buildings, with a district post housed in one school and serving all of them, and with two buildings both claiming somebody neither employs alone — and the documents do not separate those. The district’s roll-up encodes sharing a second way, in a free-text column that reads Primary School & THES, and the two encodings agree about five of the 28. Neither carries a fraction, so Carol Saranich, listed by the high school, the middle school and Turkey Hill, could be a third of a post in each or a full post in one. This is rule 11 pointed at people: a name on a list is not a share of a job, and the budget lines that pay for these posts are netted and per-district, so they cannot be split by building either. — closes: the district’s FTE-by-building assignment schedule, the sheet behind the personnel lines in the school budget.
peopleWhich fund pays which postThis is the load-bearing one. The rosters name people and the budget names dollars, and nothing published joins them to a funding source. So a paraprofessional line rising cannot be distinguished from a grant that was paying for those posts ending — which is exactly what the special education escalator rests on. — closes: DESE's End of Year Financial Report, which separates spending by fund.
peopleWhich grades Lunenburg children leave the district inDESE publishes where a town’s resident children go to school and by which route — school choice, charter, regional vocational — by receiving district and by year, FY2014 to FY2026. It does not publish that by GRADE. dese_town_enrollment carries no grade column, and the grade counts that do exist (dese_enrollment) are headcounts INSIDE a district rather than an outflow from a town, so they cannot be differenced to recover it. WHAT THIS BLOCKS: the question everyone actually asks, which is whether families leave at a transition year — entering grade 9, or entering grade 7 — or steadily throughout. Those imply completely different things about what the district could change, and the published data cannot tell them apart. IT IS NOT: an absence of evidence that transitions matter. It is an absence of evidence either way, and the plausible story (that choice-outs cluster at grade 9 when families pick a high school) is a hypothesis nothing here tests. — closes: DESE SIMS Report 7 or the district’s own October 1 enrollment submission broken out by grade and residence, which the district files annually and does not publish; or the receiving districts’ school choice enrollment by sending town and grade.
peopleWhich of DESE’s special education staff figures can be read at allEvery row of the SPECIAL EDUCATION STAFF table in yamx-769q prints an FTE, a count of students and a rate per 100 of them, so the rate has to reproduce from the other two. Recomputed for Lunenburg on every build: paraprofessionals reproduce in 8 of 8 years, teachers in 1 of 8, service FTE in 0 of 7, support FTE in 0 of 6. So three of the four rows do not describe what their own column headings say, and /how-many-students-are-on-an-iep publishes the paraprofessional row and refuses to publish the others as figures. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED is which of the three columns is the one that is wrong. — closes: DESE’s data dictionary for dataset yamx-769q, or the EPIMS aggregation behind it, stating what each column is.
peopleWhich of the district's psychologists and adjustment counselors does it report to the state as special education staff?MEASURED (sources/data/sped-definition.csv, /special-education/sped-definition): DESE counts a school psychologist or adjustment counselor as special education only under the special education job code (EPIMS 3361 and 3351, against 3360 and 3350; EOYR-EPIMS crosswalk in DESE's FY2025 printing version, rows 84 to 88). The Town's ledger carries accounts, not job codes, and the district's two End of Year Report working copies disagree: FY2023 puts every psychologist account in special education, FY2024 puts the same accounts in regular day. So psychology and guidance are left out of every special education total on this site, and the part DESE counts cannot be traced to people or accounts. — closes: the district's EPIMS staff records by job classification for its psychologists, adjustment counselors and social workers, FY2023 and FY2024.
peopleWhich of the people on the school district's master staff list still work for the districtThe district publishes its staff two ways: a sheet per building, and one master list ("Directory of Staff - All Lunenburg Public Schools Staff", a published Google Sheet). They disagree. On the 9 October 2026 fetch, 36 people appear on the master list at a building that keeps its own sheet -- 25 at the Primary School, 10 at Turkey Hill, 1 at the High School -- and that building's own sheet does not list them; a resident who knows the schools reports that at least one of them left years ago. The org chart takes each building's own sheet as the authority and sets those 36 aside, named, on the chart; it keeps 11 people the master list places district-wide or at the shared Middle/High building, marked as on that list alone. Neither list says which is current, and neither carries a start or end date. — closes: the district's current staff roster from Human Resources (or the MUNIS payroll employee list), dated.
peopleWhich posts each grant and fee fund pays for, and how much of each postThe school journal posts payroll one line per account per pay run and records no person, and grant pay posts to accounts named for a kind of work (support salaries, instructional salaries), so a grant can be totalled but not tied to a post. Year-end entries also move pay between funds, mostly citing school memos not in this archive (/school-all-funds/pay-moved-between-funds). — closes: the Town’s MUNIS payroll distribution report, each employee’s pay by fund and account, FY2023–FY2026; or the district’s grant budgets filed with DESE, which list the posts each grant pays.
peopleWhich school counselor, social-worker and psychologist posts were vacant or on leave in FY2026, and for how long?The FY2026 period-13 ledger leaves these salary lines well under budget — one psychologist account spent nothing of its budget — and no posted minutes explain it. A dollar is not a post (rule 11): vacancy, leave, a lower hiring step and contracted cover all produce the same row. One cause is on the record: on 29 July 2026 $81,075.96 moved off the high school special education resource room teacher line, and asked Was that an unfilled position?" the answer was "a leave of absence" (captions). Looking back
peopleWhich school year a printed staff roster describesThe rosters in the annual town reports carry no date, and the town’s own prose suggests the school section may run a year ahead of the cover. Three sentences in fifteen reports name a fall and a student count; matched against DESE’s October enrolment for the same school, two are closer to the year AFTER the report’s fiscal year and one to the year on the cover. So a roster labelled FY2024 may describe the autumn of 2024, which the state calls FY2025 — and any children-per-adult figure drawn from the two may be a year out of step. The FY2024 report makes the hazard concrete: it prints two complete Turkey Hill rosters, 33 names in common, one naming the leadership the town printed in FY2025 and the other the leadership it printed from FY2011 to FY2022, and neither page says which year it is. — closes: a dated staff roster, or the district’s October 1 EPIMS submission, either of which states the day the count was taken.
peopleWhich town posts are funded but standing empty?a roster names who is there and an establishment names the posts, and only the DPW and the Assessing office publish the second — so a department that shrank and a department that could not hire look identical. The Police Department’s FY27 budget presentation marks every post Funded or Funded – Vacant, which is exactly the distinction, for one department in one year — closes: the FY27 budget presentations for every department, if they all mark posts that way
peopleWho actually lives in Lunenburg — how many are over 65, how many households have a child in the schools, and what each group can afford?ANSWERED IN PART, 11 September 2026, and the part that remains is the part the argument actually runs on. The Census tables named below were fetched and are loaded as census_acs: 11,804 ± 19 residents, 1,979 ± 309 of them 65 or over, 4,529 ± 235 households, 1,477 ± 198 with a child under 18, median household income $109,753 ± $12,275 and $72,935 ± $8,677 where the householder is 65 or over. See /lunenburg-by-the-numbers, where every figure carries its margin. WHAT SURVIVES is the third clause — what each group can AFFORD. Income is not wealth, not savings, not equity and not a tax bill, and nothing published joins a property tax payment to the age of the person who paid it; the two rows below carry the two halves of what is still missing. — closes: the town census, which counts every resident by name, age and household rather than sampling them, held by the Town Clerk.
peopleWho are the ten people the Public Library employs?the Library told the town in FY2019 that it employs ten — “we only employ ten total” — and it has never printed a roster. Its annual report is signed by the Director and names a colleague only in passing prose (a Young Adult Services Librarian in FY2024, a Digital Services Librarian the same year), so the org chart holds ONE of ten. The town staff directory does not carry the Library at all: it is governed by elected Trustees rather than run from Town Hall, and has no category on lunenburgma.gov — closes: the Library’s own staff page, or the Trustees’ minutes, which record appointments
peopleWho chaired each town board after FY2016?the officials listing marked its chairs with denotes chairperson and stopped printing the footnote after FY2016; 46 bodies name a chair somewhere in their own report and 53 do not, so 218 body-years have members and nobody at the top — closes: the Town Clerk’s record of board organisational votes, which every board takes annually
peopleWho is in which of the two lists the gross wage pages print, and is anyone in both?The Calendar Year 2022 Gross Wages pages (186-192 of the FY2022 annual town report) print TWO columns, and each is alphabetised A to Z independently all the way through the seven pages -- the left column runs ABRAHAM to ZRATE across 332 names and the right BIERY to YOURK across 329. Neither is a continuation of the other, and the document puts NO HEADING over either column and no total under either, so nothing in it says what separates the two. The obvious reading -- one is the town payroll and the other the school payroll -- is a HYPOTHESIS and nothing on the page tests it. It matters because a resident adding the two columns is adding two populations they cannot name, because several surnames appear in both columns, and because the list carries no department, no position and no hours for anyone: it is 661 names and 661 gross figures. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: what the two lists are, whether any person is counted in both, and which fund paid any of it. -- closes: the Town Accountant’s payroll register for calendar year 2022 with its department and fund coding, which is the report the wage list is printed from.
peopleWho works in Accounting, Human Resources, Land Use and Facilities?the town’s own staff directory lists 29 departments and these four are in none of this project’s 61 bodies — a department that files no annual report is absent from the contents page, and one whose head is not an APPOINTED OFFICIAL is absent from the officials listing, so both our sources miss the same four. The Facilities Director is named in the FY2023 report and on the Town Office Hours page and appears in no roster — closes: the town staff directory at lunenburgma.gov/directory.aspx, whose PEOPLE tab names everyone by department
peopleWhose pay is the athletic fee fund's small regular charge in nearly every pay run, FY2023 to FY2026?MEASURED in the school journal: beside three season lumps a year, the fee fund's high school salary account (1301-3-300-3510-06-0-00-1-519999) is charged a small amount in nearly every pay run, and in FY2025 and FY2026 every such line is a whole number of half-hours at one rate ($23.77, then $24.72). Payroll posts one line per account per run and names no one. The FY26 proposed budget (26 February 2025, page 66) says the part-time athletic secretary was paid from the athletic revolving account, which fits; that it IS the secretary is our reading. Shown on /athletics/athletic-director. — closes: payroll detail by employee for the fee fund's high school salary account, FY2023 to FY2026.
peopleWhy DESE special education teacher FTE falls from 18.5 to 2.0 while total teacher FTE holds flatdese_teacher_program_area shows Lunenburg’s special education teacher FTE at 18.5 in SY2008 and 2.0 in SY2026 — a 90% collapse — while general education FTE holds between 100 and 113 and the district total is flat. A district that had lost nine tenths of its special education teachers would show it everywhere else in these files and does not. Teachers being RECODED from special education to general education produces exactly this signature. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED is that any recoding happened: a change in how FTE is apportioned when one person works across categories, a change in DESE’s program-area definitions, and a real staffing change all fit the same series. Rule 6, and nothing in the archive tests it. — closes: EPIMS work assignment records for Lunenburg aggregated by job classification and program area by year, which would show whether the same people were reported under a different code.
peopleWhy DESE’s foundation enrollment for Lunenburg at Monty Tech differs from its own October headcountTwo DESE counts of the same thing disagree in every year. The Chapter 70 foundation enrollment used to compute the assessment — derived on /monty-tech by subtracting the Lunenburg district’s from the town’s — runs between eight below and fifteen above the October headcount of Lunenburg residents attending Montachusett Regional in DESE’s own residents-by-district file, and the gap has no consistent sign or size. One documented mechanism puts children into the assessment who are not at Monty Tech: the district’s business director told the Finance Committee in March 2022 that four Lunenburg students attending trade programmes at Leominster and Nashoba “become part of the Monty Tech assessment”. That accounts for a difference in one direction and not for the years running the other way. Until it is reconciled, no per-student figure on this page can be quoted without saying which count is the denominator. — closes: DESE’s foundation enrollment detail for the Chapter 70 calculation, which states the collection date and the categories included, published beside the key factors workbook this project already holds.
peopleWhy the state’s FY2011 teacher count for Lunenburg dips and recovers a year laterDESE’s teacher file and its comparison sheet both print the FY2011 figure, and the fall shows at every one of the four schools, so it is not one school left out of the return. The state’s own total fell more that year than in any other year it publishes, which fits real cuts; but Lunenburg’s fall is among the largest in the state, and three of the four schools read higher again in FY2012. The file cannot tell a reduction restored a year later from a reporting error, so any comparison that starts in FY2011 measures the file as much as the staff. See /school-spending-history/fy2011-teacher-reading — closes: Lunenburg’s EPIMS teacher assignments by school for FY2011, or the district’s own staffing list for that school year.
recordAs of what date are the 2007 annual report's tax collection balances stated?tax-collection rows from the FY-era reports name their fiscal year. The 2007 COLLECTION OF TAXES page (PDF page 79) prints levy years from 1990 MVE to 2007 MVE and no fiscal year or as-of date anywhere on the page; the text was searched for 6/30/07, June 30, 2007 and fiscal year 2007, which appear on the balance sheet, special revenue, treasurer's, trust and debt pages but not this one. — closes: the Collector's FY2007 year-end report of committed taxes outstanding.
recordDid the town ever adopt c.32B §§21–23, the expedited plan-design route?This decides whether plan design here is bargained in full or changed through 30 days and a binding panel. §21(a) makes it a vote of the board of selectmen in a town, so Town Meeting warrants were never the place to look; no such vote has been found in the Select Board record we hold. The Board was walked through the reform and its "Maximum Possible Savings" on 22 January 2013 and the follow-ups went to executive session. — closes: the Select Board vote adopting or declining §§21–23, or a statement that none exists.
recordDoes segment 51 of a school account string mean special education?The town's account string is nine segments; the fourth is the DESE function code. The fifth is 51 on every general fund school account whose own description names special education, except special education transportation, and /analysis/special-education-costs classifies in-district special education by it -- less two accounts the district's own budget book labels as English learner costs, which shows the segment is not purely special education. The meaning of the segment is read from the account names, not from a published chart of accounts, so the in-district total rests on our reading. — closes: the Town's MUNIS chart of accounts, with the definition of each segment and its values, from the Town Accountant.
recordHow many meetings the town held, and how many of them left no record at allThis project can count meetings it has EVIDENCE of — 7,014 occasions where an agenda, a set of minutes or a recording says a board met on a day. It cannot count meetings. The town publishes documents rather than a schedule of what took place, so a meeting with no agenda, no minutes and no recording is indistinguishable from a meeting that never happened, and neither appears in sources/data/meeting-register.csv. That the gap is real rather than theoretical is shown by the meetings that survive on ONE thread: 231 occasions have a recording and no paperwork whatever, 162 of them School Committee, and 2,395 have an agenda announcing the meeting and no minutes saying what happened. Each of those would have been invisible if the other source had also been missing. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not a finding that the town met in secret. Open Meeting Law notice and the filing of minutes are separate obligations, and nothing here establishes which unrecorded meetings were noticed. — closes: the Town Clerk’s own record of meetings posted under the Open Meeting Law, which is a list of meetings NOTICED rather than a list of documents published, and is the only source that would give this register a denominator it did not derive from its own contents.
recordHow many votes each FY2027 override question received on 16 May 2026Two records disagree and neither is the certified count. The Town's unofficial tally sheet (town-supplementary/docs/town-2026-election-unofficial-results.pdf) foots precinct by precinct to its own ballots-cast total; the Division of Local Services' override record prints different yes and no counts for both questions, whose yes plus no alone exceed that ballots-cast total. Which is right is not established here. — closes: the Town Clerk's certified results of the 16 May 2026 Annual Town Election.
recordHow many weighing and measuring devices did Lunenburg's Sealer of Weights & Measures test, seal, adjust or condemn in 2009?The 2010 edition prints the Inspector of Weights & Measures' device counts and the Chapter 295 savings report (report-weights-measures). The 2009 edition prints no such report: its Textract text was searched for seal, weights, scales, condemn, savings impact and chapter 295, and returned only a receipts line SEALING FEES (p47), the appropriation and omnibus lines (p50, p73, p78), the Weights/Measures Citation Fund special revenue line (p59) and a payroll department label (p88). — closes: the Sealer's 2009 annual report to the Massachusetts Division of Standards.
recordHow many weighing and measuring devices did Lunenburg's Sealer test, seal or condemn in 2002, and what did the fees bring in?report-weights-measures holds the Sealer's device counts and fees (2010 p24-25). The 2002 Inspector of Weights and Measures reports in prose (p21) and says why there is no table: receiving no documentation or tangible evidence of previous inspections, I cannot report to you in the standard format by listing statistical data such as devices and commodities inspected. Searched: weights, sealer, sealing (pages 3, 7, 21, 47, 50, 76, 107); p47 prints SEALING FEES $568.00 as a receipt, which is the only figure. — closes: the Division of Standards' annual inspection report for Lunenburg for 2002, or the Sealer's own inspection records for that year.
recordHow many weighing and measuring devices did Lunenburg's Sealer test, seal or condemn in 2007, and what did inspection save consumers and merchants?report-weights-measures holds the Sealer's device counts and the Chapter 295 savings-impact report from the 2010 annual town report. The 2007 report's Inspector of Weights & Measures narrative (PDF page 28) says A summary sheet of devices inspected and savings to consumers and merchants impacted by this department is included in this report, but no such table is printed: Textract found no table and no text on PDF page 30 (the scan holds 67 dark pixels of 3.7 million, a blank page), and the whole text was searched for sealed, devices, savings impact and Chapter 295 -- only the narrative (p28), the SEALING FEES receipt (p57) and the omnibus Sealer line (p90) came back. — closes: the Inspector of Weights & Measures' 2007 annual report to the Division of Standards (devices sealed, by type).
recordHow many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test, seal and condemn in 2005, by device class?report-weights-measures reads the Sealer's device table (2010 pp 24-25). The 2005 Inspector of Weights & Measures report (PDF page 20) is prose only: it states The fiscal budget was $2,310 and that users were charged $3,390 in fees, and prints no device counts and no Chapter 295 savings report; the text was searched for weights, sealed, sealing and condemned (hits: pp 3, 8, 20, 54 receipts SEALING FEES, 56, 84). — closes: the Sealer of Weights & Measures' 2005 annual report to the Division of Standards.
recordHow many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test, seal, adjust or condemn in 2008, and what savings to consumers did that produce?report-weights-measures reads the Sealer's device summary and the Chapter 295 Consumer and Merchant Savings Impact Report, which the 2010 report prints at PDF pages 24-25. The 2008 Inspector of Weights and Measures report (p30) says A summary sheet of devices inspected and savings to consumers and merchants impacted by this department is included in this report, and gives only the budget ($3,350) and fees ($3,520) in prose. No such sheet is printed: the text was searched for sealed, scales, scanner, device and savings impact, and every hit is on p30's prose, a balance-sheet or warrant line (p66, p91), or the payroll. — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 2008 device inspection summary (the annual report filed with the Division of Standards).
recordHow much of what was said in a public meeting does a search of the archive actually reach?Our own text extraction inserts spaces inside words, at scale -- w ell, s elling, dep artment, B oard are all in the extracted minutes. Nine of the eleven hits for ELL are this rather than English learners. It costs twice: it manufactures tokens that were never printed, and -- the part that matters -- it makes PHRASE SEARCH MISS, because study hall broken as study h all will not match "study hall". So a search that returns nothing may mean the words were said and our copy cannot be read, which is the exact failure the coverage denominator exists to prevent, arriving underneath it. The rate has not been measured and neither has the phrase-search undercount; both are countable against the source PDFs. This belongs to extract_minutes.py, not to the index. -- closes: nothing anybody publishes. A re-extraction with a layout-aware reader, measured against the same PDFs, is the only thing that settles it.
recordIs account 8129 the Zoning Incentive Stabilization Fund or the playground fund?The annual reports print 8129 as ZONING INCENTIVE STABILIZATION (TD BANKNORTH) in FY2020 and as Zoning Stabilization Fund in FY2025. This project’s own account registry, sources/data/fund-owners.csv, records 8129 as the playground fund with its owner unresolved. Both cannot be right, and the registry is what several pages read to name an account. The extracted balances keep the document’s name and flag the disagreement rather than resolving it. — closes: the Treasurer’s chart of accounts, or the Town Meeting article that created 8129.
recordOver what period does DESE’s placement trajectory measure movementDataset 92x3-2qj9 follows a cohort from the setting its placement started in to where the same children are now, and it is the only published route into out-of-district placement. The workbook is a single Data sheet with no notes, and nothing in it or on the portal page states the interval between the start and the destination. Every rate drawn from it — including the finding that Lunenburg children who started in a substantially separate classroom are out of district about fifteen times as often as those who started in an inclusive setting — is a rate over an unstated span, so none of them can be annualised or compared with a rate measured over a known one. — closes: DESE’s methodology note for dataset 92x3-2qj9, stating the cohort rule and the interval.
recordUnder which DESE function does the district report its own function codes 2310, 2315, 2357 and 2900?The Town's account strings and the district's budget book use function codes 2310 (special education teachers, tutoring and contracted services), 2315, 2357 and 2900 (social workers), none of which is in DESE's FY2025 chart of accounts (dese-eoyr-fy2025-function-crosswalk.xlsx, sheet codes), and the FY2023 and FY2024 End of Year Report working copies print no line for them. The crosswalk compares them within their DESE group by first two digits, which is our grouping, not a published mapping. — closes: the district's worksheet mapping each MUNIS account to an End of Year Report line and program, FY2023 and FY2024.
recordWas a meeting recorded at all, when no video was posted?The video index establishes THAT a recording was posted, which is a fact the written record does not always carry — the town posts minutes for a fraction of the meetings it holds. It cannot establish the reverse: a meeting recorded and not posted, or held and not recorded, looks identical from here. — closes: the PEG station’s own cablecast log, which lists what was recorded rather than what was uploaded.
recordWhat did Ayer and Shirley each spend for each pupil BEFORE they regionalised?Ayer and Shirley regionalised for FY2012, which is the one local case anybody could learn from. The archive holds Ayer for FY2009-FY2011 and Ayer Shirley School District from FY2012, and nothing for Shirley alone beforehand - so the figure before is one town and the figure after is two. That is a different denominator, not a measured change, and comparing them would produce a confident number about the wrong thing. - closes: DESE per-pupil expenditure for Shirley, FY2009-FY2011.
recordWhat do the two Medicare plans in the FY27–FY29 PEC agreement cover?The FY27 memorandum names six plans and puts ""benefit brochures"" in Attachment A; the Attachment A received on 6 October 2026 holds four, all for active plans (Network Blue New England, Network Blue Select, Access Blue New England Saver, Blue Care Elect). Managed Blue for Seniors and Medex — the plans the memorandum sets at 75/25 and 50/50 for retirees — have only their prescription copays stated in the memorandum itself. — closes: the MIIA summaries of benefits for Managed Blue for Seniors with PDP and Medex with PDP, FY27.
recordWhat does DESE count as an “experienced” teacher in its teacher data?DESE’s teacher data prints a share of teachers it calls experienced; the workbook we hold has one sheet and no data dictionary, and no document in the archive defines the threshold. A share over a threshold also cannot see teachers moving up steps once past it. — closes: DESE’s published definition of the experienced-teacher share in its teacher data file.
recordWhat is in the PEC agreement that sets the town’s health insurance split and terms?NARROWED 6 October 2026. The PEC Agreement of 16 June 2008 is held (sources/contracts/pdf/pec-agreement-2008.pdf, a 16-page scan holding the 8-page agreement twice), received from the Town’s Human Resources Director by email. It names BCBS plans, a 75% Town share on the PPO, 80% then 75% from 1 July 2011 on the HMO and the two senior plans, 50% on Medex, 75% of the Medicare Part B premium, and a term of 1 July 2008 to 30 June 2012 continuing ""until the new agreement is reached"". What sits BETWEEN it and the FY27 memorandum, which amends ""the current in-force health insurance agreement"" without naming it, is not held: the Select Board minutes record ""the amendment dated May 14, 2013"" and a further amendment approved 11 March 2014, an agreement expiring 30 June 2016 (10 May 2016), and a Public Employee Agreement approved 12 April 2022 ""effective July 1, 2022"". Which of these the FY27 memorandum amends is not established. — closes: the complete, current agreement the Human Resources Director wrote on 6 October 2026 she was ""working on producing"", or the 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2022 instruments themselves. DECIDED 6 October 2026 (TJ): the current terms are modelled from the FY27 memorandum and its Attachments A and B, which restate every money term in full -- plans, the 75/25 and 50/50 splits, the $96 Part B payment, the $3,000/$6,000 opt-out, and the term to 30 June 2029. The missing instruments do not change any figure the model uses. They matter for the HISTORY of the split (when it moved, and to what) and for the procedural terms the memorandum carries over unrestated (eligibility, retiree and spouse definitions). Lower priority; ask when convenient.
recordWhat was actually said in the 232 executive sessions the Select Board entered citing collective bargaining?624 Select Board documents mention executive session and 232 cite collective bargaining; NO executive session minutes are in this archive. Health insurance is bargained there, so the open-session minutes catch the PEC only in passing — a phrase, an agenda line, a date — and never its substance. — closes: released executive session minutes, which the Open Meeting Law requires once the reason for secrecy has passed.
recordWhat was said at a meeting whose minutes the town published only as a photograph3,116 of the 12,015 agendas and sets of minutes this project holds (26%) contain no text a search can match. 3,096 are image scans, 3 draw their text as vector outlines, 14 are blank, 2 have a text layer our extractor could not read and 1 will not parse; a further 50 are listed by the town and not held here. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not evidence that anything was left unsaid. The words are on the page and the page is a picture of a page, so an unreadable document and a subject nobody raised produce the identical empty result. Rule 15a instructs everyone working here to search the meeting archive before concluding a thing was never discussed, and until this was measured that search silently skipped a quarter of the record while printing a coverage line saying otherwise. IT IS NOT EVEN: the coverage is not evenly spread, so an archive-wide figure understates the boards that carry it — Board of Assessors 255 of 488 (52%); Select Board 629 of 1,347 (47%); Lunenburg Housing Authority 110 of 255 (43%). Measured per board and year in sources/data/minutes-searchable.csv, which scripts/build_minutes_searchable.py regenerates and check_generated.py refuses to let go stale. — closes: OCR of the image-only documents, already on the roadmap in notes/QUEUE.md, which recovers the scans and the vector-outline pages but produces OUR rendering rather than the town's own words (rule 13) and so must never be quoted as the document's text; and, for the documents the town lists that we do not hold, a records request to the Town Clerk for the minutes of the named meetings in a text-bearing format.
recordWhat was the School Committee told under "FY26 Year End Budget review" on 2 and 9 September 2026?Both agendas carry the item (Old Business, 5 minutes). The archive's catalogue of the Town's AgendaCenter lists no minutes for either meeting, so the only written statement on the FY26 school year-end held here is the 29 July 2026 minutes, in which the business manager was "confident the remaining amount would be well below" the approximately $600,000 returned in FY25. The machine captions of the recordings can locate a moment but are not a record. /analysis/fy26-school-surplus. — closes: the approved School Committee minutes of 2 and 9 September 2026, and any year-end budget document presented under that item.
recordWhen the town actually POSTED each agenda and each set of minutes — the two timestamps the Open Meeting Law turns on (48 hours of notice; minutes in a timely way)The AgendaCenter publishes no posting timestamp and our watch was seeded on 8 September 2026, so only 24 of 12,089 documents have a first-seen date. The documents’ own creation timestamps (sources/data/meeting-document-timestamps.csv) bound the posting from below and cannot prove when a file went up, and a file replaced in place takes a new date — closes: an AgendaCenter export carrying the posted-on date per document, or the town’s own record of when each was uploaded.
recordWhen the town actually posted an agenda or a set of minutes, as against when we first saw itThe AgendaCenter lists a document's MEETING date and publishes no posting date anywhere -- not in the listing markup, not in the file's URL, not in the response headers. So scripts/watch_meetings.py can record only first_seen, the day this project's crawler first observed a document, and the gap between a meeting and its minutes appearing is bounded by how often we look rather than measured. Every such field in sources/data/meeting-watch-events.csv and in fy28/public/data/meeting-feed.json is named days_after_meeting_upper_bound for that reason. WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not a measurement of how long the town takes, and a document posted the day after a meeting and one posted three weeks later are indistinguishable if we looked once in between. It is also blind backwards: the 12,065 documents the watch adopted when it was seeded on 8 September 2026 carry no first_seen at all -- an empty cell rather than a guess -- so no lag figure exists for anything published before that date, and the series begins the day the watch did. The separate question of how many meetings the town HELD is registered above, “How many meetings the town held, and how many of them left no record at all”. -- closes: the CivicEngage AgendaCenter's own record of when each document was uploaded, which the platform stores and the public listing does not render; the Town Clerk or the site administrator can export it.
recordWhen was a meeting recording made, where the title does not say?The PEG channel’s video titles are the only chronology there is: a flat channel extraction returns no upload dates, and 652 of the 4,671 titles state no date at all (as indexed 8 September 2026). For those the recording can be placed only by its position in the channel listing, which is not a date. — closes: the channel’s own per-video publication date, which the YouTube Data API returns as snippet.publishedAt. Even that is an UPLOAD date and not the meeting date.
recordWhether Lunenburg’s MCAS results are high or low for MassachusettsResidents have argued the comparison in both directions at School Committee — that the town is “in the top 20% for school performance while being in the bottom 10% for spending”, and that “neighboring districts… have faced similar challenges while achieving stronger outcomes”. The spending half of that can be checked here, because DESE publishes the statewide distribution of per-pupil spending with quartiles and a rank. The results half cannot: this archive holds MCAS for six districts and no statewide distribution of it at all, so no percentile, rank or state median can be computed for any of the four measures. — closes: DESE’s district-level MCAS achievement file for all districts, published per year at profiles.doe.mass.edu, extracted the way the finance distribution already is.
recordWhether a board discussed a thing at a meeting it noticed but left no minutes and no recording of1,754 of the 6,990 meetings in sources/data/meeting-register.csv (25%) have a posted AGENDA and neither minutes nor a recording, so the only surviving record is that the meeting was noticed and what it meant to take up. 235 of them are since 1 July 2024. It is worst where a body is small: School Advisory Councils & Committees 229 of 268 (85%), Capital Planning 63 of 182 (35%), Board of Health 101 of 297 (34%). WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not evidence that nothing was discussed, and a search that returns nothing for one of these dates has not searched the meeting -- it has searched an agenda. The practical cost is the inverse question. Parks Commission can be shown DISCUSSING its budget (44 of 192 meeting dates carry the word, and Budget / Finance Review is a named agenda item from 22 July 2026), and cannot be shown NOT to have, because 40 of its 193 meetings left no account at all -- including 30 September 2026, whose agenda item was Budget Check-in. This is distinct from the register's own limit, that a meeting with no agenda either is indistinguishable from one never held: here the town has published a notice, so the meeting is established and only its content is missing. — closes: the minutes themselves. G.L. c.30A §22 requires a public body to create and maintain accurate minutes of every meeting and to make them available on request, so for each of these dates the document is owed whether or not it was ever posted to the AgendaCenter. Requested by board and date.
recordWhich body met, for a recording whose title names none?14 of 4,671 videos are undetermined — Informational Symposium, Lunenburg Town Charrette . FULL, Master Plan Public Forum, School Funding Forum, 911 YouTube. The title is all we fetch; the channel also carries a description field on each video and several of these titles say "See Description". — closes: the per-video description text from the channel, which the index does not currently store.
recordWhich capital project is the unnamed $25,000.00 on the FY2016 capital projects schedule?THE PAGE PRINTS A RULED ROW WITH A FIGURE AND NO NAME. On CAPITAL PROJECT FUNDS FY 2016, PDF page 36 of the FY2016 annual town report, the row between the column header and 08/02 ATM Development of Cemeteries carries $25,000.00 in APPROPRIATED FORWARD and nothing else -- no purpose, no article reference, no fwd flag, no expended figure, no balance. IT IS NOT A READING ERROR AND IT IS NOT IGNORABLE. All three columns of the page tie to the printed Grand Total to the cent only when that $25,000.00 is counted, so the figure is part of the schedule. And the Cemeteries row immediately below it does not close as printed -- $1,019.01 less $35,229.38 is ($34,210.37) against a printed balance of ($9,210.37), short by exactly $25,000.00. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: that the $25,000.00 belongs to the Cemeteries project. A label that failed to print, a second article against the same project, and a separate project whose text was lost all fit the same evidence, and nothing in the report tests between them. — closes: the Town Accountant's FY2016 capital project fund detail by article, which names the article every capital appropriation sits under.
recordWhich figure did the 2018 Annual Town Meeting actually vote where the printed FY 2019 Omnibus Budget does not add up?The budget as printed on pages 155-158 of the FY2018 annual town report carries TWO arithmetic misprints and the document contradicts itself about both. Total General Government $1,401,119.25 is 709.00 MORE than the 22 lines beneath it, and the printed Total Omnibus $36,804,408.83 agrees with the subtotal rather than with the lines. Total Assistance $243,493.56 is 2,000.00 LESS than the two subtotals above it, and there the Total Omnibus agrees with the subtotals rather than with the line. Ten of the twelve section totals foot their own line items to the cent, every subtotal foots exactly, and the pages carry a digital text layer, so this is the town's arithmetic and not our reading. What a resident cannot tell from the published report is which number was put to the meeting: the appropriation is voted as one sum, and a 709.00 or 2,000.00 difference changes what the departments beneath it were authorised to spend. - closes: the Town Clerk's certified record of the vote on Article 7 of the 5 May 2018 Annual Town Meeting, which states the sum voted and the schedule attached to it.
recordWhich figure did the 2019 Annual Town Meeting vote for Central Purchasing, where the printed FY 2020 Omnibus Budget prints two that are a factor of ten apart?The budget is printed on pages 161-164 of the FY2019 annual town report (printed pages 159-162) and the document contradicts itself in two places. p162 prints 38 Central Purchasing $ 603,030.00 and, three rows beneath it, Total Central Purchasing $ 60,303.00 -- $542,727.00 apart. And p162 prints four Fire lines (1,093,374.24 + 20,000.00 + 15,000.00 + 10,000.00 = 1,138,374.24) above Subtotal Fire Dept. $1,138,434.24, $60.00 more than its own lines. Sixteen of the eighteen printed group totals foot their own line items to the cent and the twelve section totals sum to the printed Total Omnibus $38,058,164.30 exactly, so this is the town's arithmetic and not our reading: both pairs were read at 400 dpi off the page's own bitmap. The town's grand total is footed on $60,303.00 and on $1,138,434.24, so the printed Total Omnibus cannot distinguish a misprinted line from a misprinted subtotal. A resident cannot tell from the published report what Central Purchasing was authorised to spend in FY2020, and the two readings differ by more than half a million dollars. -- closes: the Town Clerk's certified record of the vote on the FY2020 omnibus budget article at the 2019 Annual Town Meeting, with the schedule attached to the motion as moved.
recordWhich fiscal year did Town Meeting vote the left-hand half of the FY 2016 Omnibus Budget for?The omnibus schedule on pages 140-141 of the FY2015 annual town report is titled FY 2016 Omnibus Budget and is set as two panels per page. Its right panel is headed VOTED FY 2016 and its left panel VOTED FY 2015. Everything else on the page says it is one column: the line numbers run 1 to 82 continuously across both panels and both pages, the 91 line items sum exactly to the single TOTAL OMNIBUS of $32,025,895.00, and so do the twelve printed section totals. But the report itself never states which heading is wrong, and the arithmetic cannot tell a misprinted heading from a correct one. Until it is settled, no figure from the left panel may be cited as an FY2015 appropriation or as an FY2016 one without saying which. - closes: the Town Clerk's record of the vote at the 2015 Annual Town Meeting, with the warrant article and the amount as moved, which the town holds and does not publish.
recordWho appoints each appointed official, and to whom do they answer?the annual report heads six pages APPOINTED OFFICIALS and names nobody as the appointing authority, so a Constable, a Town Clockwinder and a Wellness Coordinator sit in the record with no department and no stated superior. The town charter is the document that says which appointments belong to the Select Board and which to the Town Manager, and this archive does not hold it — closes: the Lunenburg town charter and the general bylaws
recordWhy DESE’s FY2025 transportation spending for Lunenburg differs from the town ledgerDESE's End of Year Financial Report gives general fund in-district transportation (function 3300) and out-of-district transportation, and their sum equals the town's MUNIS regular plus special education transportation accounts to the dollar in FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024. In FY2025 DESE's sum is higher than the ledger and nothing published explains it. In FY2020 and FY2021 the two differ by equal and opposite amounts, which is what one payment booked in different years by the two would look like. — closes: the district's FY2025 End of Year Financial Report workpapers mapping MUNIS accounts to DESE functions, from the Business Office.
recordWhy does the FY2024 End of Year Report working copy repeat FY2023's special education figures for guidance, psychology and two substitute lines?MEASURED (sources/data/sped-definition.csv, checked by scripts/build_sped_crosswalk.py): five Special Education cells of the FY2024 working copy (eoy24!F173, F178, F258, F262 and F274) equal the FY2023 copy's to the dollar, and the psychology figure matches no FY2024 ledger account while the FY2024 psychologist salaries sit, whole, in the Regular Day column. Whether the five were carried forward unchanged, or the report as filed differs, is not stated in the working copy. — closes: the FY2024 End of Year Financial Report as filed with DESE.
recordWhy the FY2023 annual town report and the school journal disagree, fund by fund, on special education grant spendingMEASURED (/special-education/special-education-overruns, the ten-year table): for FY2023 the annual town report's Special Revenue Funds schedule prints disbursements of $562,063.28 from the special education grant funds and the school journal posts $560,954.43 to the same grants (payments plus what was still owed) -- $1,108.85 apart in total, while the circuit breaker account (fund 2640) agrees to the cent, $494,967.72. Fund by fund the gap is larger and runs both ways: the FY2022 #240 grant is $10,495.25 higher in the journal, the FY2023 #240 grant $3,564.68 higher, the FY2021 #240 grant $670.67 lower, and the report prints two #262 rows ($12,500.00 and $1,998.11) the journal has no FY2023 postings for. The page uses the report's disbursements for FY2017-FY2022, where no journal is held. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the difference is timing (cash paid against obligations recorded), grant-year attribution, or a transcription in one of the two. -- closes: the Town Accountant's FY2023 trial balance for the school grant funds, showing expenditures and encumbrances by fund.
recordWhy the IDEA grant stopped being booked to the teaching and materials headings in FY2025MEASURED in the school MUNIS journal (/school-all-funds/grant-coding): every IDEA entitlement grant from FY2021 to FY2024 posted its spending to function 2300 or 2400 -- headings that name teaching and instructional materials but no single voted line. The FY2025 grant posted most of its spending to 0000, no function at all, and the FY2026 grant to 2000, the instruction heading. The ledger records the change and not the reason: a new account set-up, a change of staff in the business office, or a decision to code at the grant level all fit the same postings. — closes: the business office's account set-up for each IDEA grant, FY2023-FY2026, and the IDEA budgets the district filed with DESE by function code.
recordWhy these six districts and not six othersEvery comparison on this page runs against a set of six districts chosen by this project — Ashburnham-Westminster, Ayer Shirley, Groton-Dunstable, Harvard, North Middlesex and Lunenburg. DESE’s RADAR workbook covers all 421 Massachusetts districts and this archive extracts six because the full file takes the published database past Cloudflare’s per-asset limit. No document here records the criterion by which those six were picked, and a peer set is an argument: whoever chooses it has already made a claim about what Lunenburg is comparable to. That is why every headline figure on /what-other-districts-spend is stated against DESE’s statewide distribution of 318 districts rather than against the six. — closes: DESE’s own DART comparison group for Lunenburg, which names the districts the Department considers similar and states the criteria it used.
studentsHow many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in 1987?placement-counts holds this from the Special Services report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual town reports. The 1987 annual town report mentions special education only as programs inside the schools (a Special Needs Language Class and two self-contained classes, text lines 7088-7267) and prints no count of out-of-district placements. Searched for special education, special needs, placement, tuition and 766 (sources/data/report-tables/1987/). — closes: the School Department's October 1987 count of placements by type, or the Department of Education's fiscal 1987 end-of-year report.
studentsHow many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in the 1973-74 school year?placement-counts holds out-of-district placements from FY2013 onward. The 1974 report predates a placement count: it describes Chapter 766 as a new law (p89, p95, p98) and lists Aid to Special Classes, Chapter 69 as a receipt (p147), with no count of children placed outside the district. Searched placed out, out-of-district, Chapter 766 and special class (sources/data/report-tables/1974/). — closes: the DESE end-of-year pupil report for 1973-74.
studentsHow many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in the 1978-79 school year?placement-counts holds this from the Special Services report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual town reports. The 1979 report's Special Needs Director's report (pp113-114) describes the Chapter 766 program, aides, screening and counselling in prose and prints no placement count; the only mention of out-of-district placements is a sentence thanking the teachers of children in out-of-district placements and in home tutoring (p114). Searched placement, 766 and out-of-district across all pages (sources/data/report-tables/1979/). — closes: DESE's SIMS Report 7 for Lunenburg for school year 1978-79, or the Special Needs Director's placement list.
studentsHow many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in the 2002 school year?placement-counts holds this from the Special Services report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual town reports. The 2002 annual town report prints no Lunenburg Special Services report and no placement count: its Textract text was searched for special services, special education, SIMS and placement; special services hits only Monty Tech's own section (p32), special education hits Monty Tech (p32, p34), a high-school staff heading (p40) and a state assessment line (p54), SIMS hits nothing, and placement hits a senior job-placement programme and a library site ranking (p15) besides 19 instances of replacement (sources/data/report-tables/2002/). — closes: DESE's SIMS placement report for Lunenburg for 2001-02, or the district's own Special Services annual report for 2002.
studentsHow many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in the 2010 school year?placement-counts holds this from the Special Services report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual town reports. The 2010 annual town report prints no Special Services report and no placement count: its Textract text was searched for special services, special education, SIMS and placement, and returned only a coordinator's name and a retirement notice (sources/data/report-tables/2010/). — closes: DESE's SIMS placement report for Lunenburg for 2009-10, or the district's own Special Services annual report for 2010.
studentsHow many children were enrolled in each Lunenburg school, by grade, on October 1, 2004?report-enrollment-mcas holds an enrollment-by-school-and-grade table from the 2010 annual town report (p34). The 2004 annual town report prints none: its Textract text was searched for enrollment, enrolment, October 1 and students across all 112 pages. The hits are prose: p32 gives Monty Tech's October 1, 2004 enrollment by member town (Lunenburg 59), and p45 gives the Elementary and Primary Schools a combined enrollment of six hundred thirty students. No count by school and grade for the district. — closes: DESE's October 1, 2004 enrollment report for Lunenburg by school and grade (SIMS), or the district's own October 1 report for 2004-05.
studentsHow many of the children counted as leaving a Lunenburg school moved out of townAttrition is leaving for ANY reason, so a family that moves to another state and a family that keeps its address and enrolls a child elsewhere are the same number. Without the split, the rate cannot be read as a statement about the schools at all -- and it is the reading every resident supplies. The town's own records could bound it: residency is what the district verifies at enrollment and what the assessor's and clerk's records track. — closes: the district's withdrawal records coded by reason (moved out of district / transferred within Massachusetts / private / home school), which is a field SIMS already requires the district to report on every exit.
studentsHow were Lunenburg's out-of-district special education placements in 2003-04 split between collaborative, day and residential programmes, and on what date were they counted?placement-counts splits each year's count three ways from the SIMS-sourced Special Services report (FY2013-FY2025). The 2003 annual town report prints a count in prose only (p46, Special Services Report: only eight students receive services outside the district during the 2003/2004 school year, and 245 students receiving special education or related services), with no split, no count date and no source: its text was searched for special services, special education, SIMS, placement, collaborative and residential (sources/data/report-tables/2003/). — closes: DESE's SIMS placement report for Lunenburg for 2003-04.
studentsWhich school a Lunenburg student who left went to, by gradeDESE publishes two files that each hold half of this and never the join. dese_attrition gives an attrition rate for every grade, every year, and names no destination. dese_residents_sending names every receiving district and the reason -- Monty Tech, school choice, charter, foster care -- and carries no grade at all. So the single largest measured departure in this town, about one in five of every eighth grade, cannot be attributed to anywhere: a vocational admission, a private school, a charter, a school choice transfer, an out-of-district placement and a family moving out of town are one number. — closes: one column. DESE's residents-sending file with a grade on each row, or the district's own October SIMS submission broken out by exit grade and exit reason, which the district files to the state every 1 October and does not report to its own School Committee.
studentsWhy one in five Lunenburg eighth graders does not return for grade 9The rate is measured and stable across seventeen years, two building reorganisations and a pandemic. The reason is not measured anywhere. Monty Tech admits at grade 9 and Lunenburg is a member town there, so a child going there moves part of the town's bill rather than adding to it -- but nothing published links the two quantities, and the same rate is equally consistent with private and parochial admission at grade 9, with charter admission, with an out-of-district special education placement made at the transition, and with families moving. — closes: nothing anybody currently publishes. The nearest thing is an exit survey or an exit-reason tally kept by the district at the point a student is withdrawn, which is a record the district could choose to keep and report and does not.
town-meetingDid Town Meeting vote the 2014 increase in the senior tax work-off cap from $750 to $1,000?The committee voted on 27 January 2014 to take it to Town Meeting; the May 2014 Annual Town Meeting proceedings in the FY2014 annual report carry no such article. -- closes: the 2014 Annual and Special Town Meeting warrants and the Town Clerk's proceedings
town-meetingWhat did Town Meeting vote before May 2011?The archive's record of Town Meeting votes is the Town Clerk's printed proceedings in the annual town reports, and the earliest report it holds is FY2011, so /town-meeting-votes begins with the 7 May 2011 Annual Town Meeting. Nothing earlier is missing from the page by choice; it is not in the archive. — closes: the annual town reports for FY2010 and earlier, or the Town Clerk's certified record of each earlier Town Meeting.
town-meetingWhat did the Town Clerk record for the 2026 Town Meetings, and for the warrant articles the extracted Clerk's record does not reach?Results for the May and September 2026 meetings come only from our reading of the meeting videos, because the annual town report that prints the Clerk's record of them is not yet in the archive. For FY2015 onward the Clerk's record as extracted (town-meeting-votes.csv) also does not reach every article on the posted warrant; /town-meeting-votes counts the shortfall year by year. Either the Clerk's pages print fewer articles or our extraction missed them, and nothing here yet tells which. — closes: the FY2026 annual town report's Town Clerk section, and a page-by-page re-read of the Clerk's proceedings in the FY2015-FY2025 reports.
town-meetingWhat exactly did the warrants of the May 2025 Annual, the November 2025 Special, the August 2016 Special and every Town Meeting from 2011 to 2014 ask, article by article, and what did the Clerk record for the 38 votes printed without a meeting date?The archive holds no warrant booklet for those meetings, so their articles are known only from the Town Clerk's record in the annual report (a summary of each vote) and, from 2021, our notes of the recordings; and the FY2011-FY2013 reports print 38 votes under headings with no date. — closes: the posted warrant for each meeting, and the Clerk's dated proceedings for FY2011-FY2013.
town-meetingWhen did Town Meeting accept the senior tax work-off program (c.59 s.5K), and by what vote?The annual reports print "Est. 1998", the Town Manager told the Select Board May 2000 (5 March 2019), and the town's 2021 policy leaves the date blank. -- closes: the Town Clerk's certified copy of the acceptance vote

Examples — real questions, run against the live database

Every query below is run against the live database when this page is built, so a question that stops answering breaks the build rather than sitting here looking answerable. Two of them return nothing, and that is the honest state of the archive rather than a fault.

partlyEvery source of revenue in FY2022, by name and amount, with our classification
SELECT fy, printed_name, label, class, amount, document, page FROM revenue_history WHERE fy = 2022 ORDER BY amount DESC

class says what KIND of revenue it is — levy, state aid, local receipt, transfer — which is a property of where the money came FROM. It does not say what the money went on to pay for, and for anything landing in the general fund nothing can: that money is fungible by law and no document apportions it. Only restricted funds have a traceable destination, and those are in money_edges.

The classification is joined in at build time from money_classification, so the name the report printed and the group we assigned are in one row.

not yetThe same question for FY2023
SELECT fy, printed_name, amount FROM revenue_history WHERE fy = 2023

0 rows

Returns nothing, and that is the correct answer rather than a failure. revenue_history carries only years whose extract was CHECKED against the report’s own printed total. FY2023 has 10 unchecked rows in annual_report_receipts; loading them here would make five verified years and one guess look identical.

answersWhat was budgeted for the Superintendent, FY2022 to FY2025
SELECT fy, stage, label, value FROM budget_figure WHERE label LIKE '%Superintendent%' AND fy BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025 ORDER BY fy, stage

One row per stage, and they are different quantities: proposed is what was asked for, settled what was voted, actual what the later document reported. Rule 1 — never compute a growth rate from one stage to another.

budget_figure is one row per line × year × stage × variant. Filtering on a label works here because "Superintendent" is unique; most lines are not, which is what line_key is for.

FY2024 has no settled stage in the archive — only proposed and actual. So this is what the district ASKED for that year, not what the town voted. The stage you get is not the stage you named, and the coverage table below is the only place that difference is visible before you query.

Which stages exist varies by year, so a query written for one year can silently return nothing for another.

period is a point in time inside the year, not a stage. Two periods of the same year are two different MUNIS reports and adding them double-counts.

The S prefix is the structural way to find school accounts — it does not depend on any name, and MUNIS names are ten characters typed by a person.
